jobs.title: Sustainability Manager - Maternity Leave Cover
jobs.excerpt: The RSB - Roundtable on Sustainable Biomaterials Association - seeks an independent consultant for a maternity leave coverage period to support a growing portfolio of work in GHG accounting, corporate Scope 3 emission reporting, environmental attribute accounting (i.
jobs.description:
The RSB - Roundtable on Sustainable Biomaterials Association - seeks an independent consultant for a maternity leave coverage period to support a growing portfolio of work in GHG accounting, corporate Scope 3 emission reporting, environmental attribute accounting (i.e. book and claim systems) in the context of sustainable materials, chemicals and fuels. Subject to organisational needs, funding availability and mutual interest, this engagement may create opportunities for future employment.

About Us

Our growing, dedicated team of committed professionals works globally to develop solutions to some of the world’s biggest challenges. We operate remotely in many countries worldwide, with a robust and collaborative working environment fostering professional development and a healthy work-life balance. Our team allows for individual autonomy and the opportunity to engage with a full spectrum of roles within our stakeholder base's diverse range of organisations.

RSB is a global, multi-stakeholder organisation dedicated to driving the sustainable development of the bioeconomy based on our best-in-class sustainability framework. Frequently noted as industry leaders in navigating the complexities of supply chain sustainability, we take pride in applying our robust sustainability framework in diverse sectors, including aviation, chemicals, materials, and shipping.

For more information, visit

Your Role

As Sustainability Manager, you will play a key role in supporting RSB member and non-member clients by delivering projects to accelerate the sustainable transition to circular bio-economy in different business industries and across different topics.

You will report to the Director of Advisory Services and the Sustainability Manager GHG expert, and work closely with the other RSB areas, such as the Programs, Sustainability Foundations, and RSB Secretariat teams.

You will be responsible for these main areas of work:

Project Delivery

Contribute to RSB’s Advisory Services Projects assigned to you, including operational, administrative, engagement and content development activities. Support the delivery of multiple client-facing projects based on sustainable feedstocks, biofuels, traceability (incl. Book and Claim systems), and other standard and certification related topics with a special focus on GHG emission savings and LCA approach. This includes but is not limited to:

  • Support the delivery of multiple projects, including their work packages and tasks in compliance with contract timelines and due dates. Develop reports and practical guidelines to document project findings, including results in slide decks for presentation to internal and external clients. Develop training content to diverse audiences.
  • Lead, conduct and coordinate LCA and GHG assessments based on relevant regulatory and standard requirements and methodologies, including (but not limited to) RSB, CORSIA, and EU RED.
  • Support internal and external knowledge needs on cross-cutting LCA GHG emissions related themes with technical expertise, covering different topics such as feedstocks, bioenergy processes, bioplastics and emerging technologies (e.g., Power-to-X) tied to different sectors (e.g., aviation, fuels and chemicals).
  • Support the development and updates of RSB LCA GHG methodologies and contribute to improvements and updates to RSB’s GHG Tool and Standards from a GHG perspective.
  • Conduct literature reviews, benchmarks and gap analysis with existing sustainability standards, policies and guidance, touching on bioenergy products and alternative materials.
  • Support research on feedstock alternatives, their selection and responsible sourcing of alternative materials, including analysis of trade-offs with other environmental and social impacts, supply chain mapping and land use issues (e.g. degraded land and ILUC).
  • Where applicable, facilitate stakeholder engagement processes to ensure robustness and social validation of specific proposals, ensuring engagement records are well documented and up to date.
  • Familiarize with RSB standard and certification mechanisms and frameworks, including RSB’s proprietary tools to assess environmental and social risks.

Proposal Development

Contribute to ongoing and future advisory services projects related to biomaterials, by supporting efforts in engaging with clients, identifying their needs and developing proposals according to RSB’s templates, in topics related to:

  • Feedstock Assessments.
  • Conceptual frameworks on feedstock processing to biofuels and / or biomaterials.
  • LCA GHG assessments, including calculations and LCA implementation analysis as aligned to applicable regulatory frameworks.
  • Certification and Standard benchmarks and gap analyses.
  • Training activities.

Administrative and Management Requirements

Support Advisory Services area in the need of tracking, documenting, archiving, and completing proposal and project related information, including:

  • Concept note and proposal templates.
  • Contract follow-up, project data updates and invoice tracking.
  • Proposal and Project documentation, including digital folder updates.
  • Data completion on support digital platforms.
  • Where applicable, coordinate with external consultants involved in supporting on-going project delivery.
  • Other activities as deemed relevant to Advisory Services purposes, and support to other functional areas if required.

Requirements

Required - Education, experience, and qualifications

  • Master's degree or equivalent experience in environmental science, environmental engineering, or a related field.
  • 10+ years of relevant professional experience.
  • Demonstrated expertise in LCA GHG calculation and assessment methodologies.
  • Experience leading the implementation of complex projects.
  • Experience working in one or more of the following sectors:
    • Bioenergy / Biofuels
    • Chemicals and materials
  • Strong analytical and technical writing skills.
  • Fluency in English.
  • Effective project communication skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office software.

Required - Personal attributes

  • Ability to translate complex technical issues into practical business recommendations.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote, international environment.
  • Comfortable operating in evolving methodological landscapes.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to scientific rigor.
  • Excellent project management and prioritization skills.
  • Resilience under strict project due dates and the ability to manage client needs.
  • Interest in market transformation, sustainable fuels, and high-integrity climate solutions.
  • Strong interpersonal skills.

Desired

  • Experience with regulatory frameworks, including EU-RED and CORSIA systems, sustainability standards, renewable energy certificates, (e.g., SAF certificates).
  • Knowledge of broadly accepted GHG methodologies and tools.
  • Familiarity with sustainability certification systems such as RSB.
  • Experience working with multinational companies on climate strategy or sustainability reporting.

While we welcome the use of tools to support your application process, we strongly encourage candidates to submit their own original responses in the cover letter and application questions. Due to the high volume of applications and the increasing similarity of AI-generated responses, it can be difficult to accurately assess and distinguish individual candidates. We therefore encourage you to share your personal experiences, motivations, and perspectives in your own words.

Benefits

Our benefits

  • Competitive salary (according to EU regulations we need to say a range)
  • Flexible working hours
  • Remote work in home-office with periodic in-person team meetings
  • Professional development opportunities

Important information

  • Location: The position is home office-based. Candidates must be located in Spain and possess a valid work permit for the country.
  • Travel: Required for meetings several times per year.
  • Position type: Full-time.
  • Duration: Temporary maternity cover, anticipated to last between 7 to 9 months. The actual duration will depend on the employee’s leave and return date. The position cover may start up to 15 days before the leave for handover.
  • Start Date: October 2026
  • Application Deadline: 28th September 2026

Please provide a Cover Letter describing why you wish to work with us and why you are the right fit, and a CV of no more than two to three pages. RSB will not consider applications that do not follow these steps.

About the Role

We are searching for a results-driven VP of Enterprise Sales to lead and grow a team of enterprise sales reps selling our AI-powered SaaS underwriting and analytics solutions to health insurance and benefits organizations. In this role, you’ll own your team's pipeline, forecasting, and quota attainment while instilling a consultative selling mindset across the group. The ideal candidate has led or coached sales teams before, brings credibility across the health insurance ecosystem, and has experience rolling out new sales methodologies that actually stick. They thrive coaching reps through complex, multi-stakeholder deals and are comfortable representing their team's results to leadership.

How You Will Make an Impact

  • Recruit, coach, and manage a team of enterprise sales reps, setting clear expectations around pipeline, forecasting, and consultative selling standards
  • Own regional sales targets, ensuring the team hits, achieves, and exceeds monthly and annual quotas, with accurate forecasting and pipeline reporting in Salesforce
  • Conduct regular 1:1s and pipeline reviews with each rep to identify coaching opportunities, remove blockers, and reinforce consultative selling as the standard, not a one-time initiative
  • Lead by example on key deals, stepping into complex or strategic opportunities to model consultative selling and build credibility with major accounts
  • Own hiring, onboarding, and ramp planning for new reps joining the team
  • Identify underperformance early and create improvement plans, while recognizing and developing high performers on the team
  • Partner with Marketing, Product, and Customer Success to relay field feedback and help shape regional demand generation and messaging
  • Represent the team in leadership forecasting calls and QBRs, providing visibility into regional trends, risks, and opportunities

Skills Needed to Succeed

  • 10+ years of enterprise SaaS or technology sales experience, including experience leading, coaching, or mentoring a sales team
  • Domain expertise in the health insurance space
  • Proven experience hiring, onboarding, and developing sales talent, including identifying and addressing underperformance
  • A strong consultative and strategic mindset with prior experience rolling out a new sales process or methodology across a team
  • Ideally prior experience navigating complex buying committees, including Chief Actuaries, CMOs, VPs of Underwriting, and CFOs at health carriers and benefits organizations
  • Outstanding verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to lead in a self-driven manner within a fast-paced, collaborative startup environment; comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward action

What We Offer:

  • A fun, team-oriented startup culture.
  • Generous stock options - we all get to own a piece of what we’re building.
  • Unlimited vacation days.
  • Flexible schedule that supports working from home.
  • Full benefits package includes medical, dental, vision, 401k, paid paternal leave, and more.
  • Ample opportunities to learn and take on new responsibilities.

We are an equal opportunity employer.

This role is also eligible for commission, equity grant and a comprehensive benefits package. Modern Health is a mental health benefits platform for employers. We are energized by bringing together the best talent in the industry to achieve audacious goals focused on making mental health a strength and priority for all.

The Role:

Maintaining the security and privacy of our users is paramount to Modern Health’s mission. As a member of the security team you will have organization-wide visibility to continuously support and monitor our commitment to privacy, security, and compliance.

This is a unique opportunity to use your engineering and security skills to make a direct impact in people's lives. We need a security engineer who can pick up and understand complex technical areas quickly, mitigate risk by increasing automation in security domains, and work with other engineers to securely release and maintain software, infrastructure, and an information security management system, while always working to increase our security and compliance posture.

This role will be part of the Product Security (ProdSec) team, report to the Head of Security, and can be based anywhere in the United States. This is a unique opportunity to be a security leader at a fast growing company, and the work done by this position will lay the foundation for security at Modern Health for years to come!

You will:

  • Participate in collaborative threat modeling initiatives for new features and evolving services, ensuring proactive risk identification and reduction.
  • Conduct secure code reviews on services and applications built with modern frameworks and technologies.
  • Assist in planning and executing targeted penetration tests on new features, identifying and reporting vulnerabilities before production release.
  • Collaborate on IT security initiatives, partnering with infrastructure and operations teams to review security controls for device management, endpoint protection, access management, and overall IT hygiene.
  • Engage with Cloud Security efforts by partnering with DevOps and Infrastructure teams to assess, improve, and monitor cloud architecture, security policies, and cloud-native controls to ensure secure deployment and operations of applications and services.

We are looking for a Sales Strategy & Operations Manager to support our Strategic segment — the largest and most complex fleets in our market, where a single account can represent millions in ARR and a multi-year, multi-product relationship. Your ability to think strategically, adapt quickly, and get things done will earn credibility with all levels of the organization. You will collaborate closely with Strategic Sales Leadership, the Enterprise Sales Operations team, and the broader Go-to-Market organization, and will direct analytical support from our Strategy & Operations team in Pakistan.

  • Own territory design and book-of-business optimization, moving from one-size-fits-all account counts to a variable model that reflects account potential, incumbent providers, and industry focus

  • Exceptional spreadsheet and data management skills to quickly structure analyses, answer key business questions, and drive decision making
  • Experience in building Salesforce reports and dashboards, knowledge in how SFDC applications integrate with each other, and ability to enable sales on SFDC best practices and related tools
  • Experience partnering with Sales Leadership on initiatives such as weekly forecasting, territory alignment, ROE, QBRs and other related projects

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Excel and Google Sheets expertise is a must; SQL proficiency and hands-on experience in a notebook-based analytics tool such as Hex querying a cloud data warehouse such as Snowflake is strongly preferred

About Alma Lasers

Alma, a Sisram Medical company, is a global leader in medical-aesthetic technologies with over 25 years of experience in energy-based devices (EBD). Operating in more than 100 countries worldwide, Alma combines advanced technology, clinical expertise, and a holistic approach to aesthetic and wellness care.

The primary responsibility of the Field Service Technician II is to travel to customer sites throughout the continental United States with East Coast focus and provide repairs to Alma Lasers equipment and complete Preventative Maintenance as scheduled. This position will sometimes provide level two technical trouble shooting with customers via phone.

Come be a part of the amazing culture here at Alma!

  • Read diagrams and schematics to perform full board swaps as needed
  • Test machines after repair to ensure proper functionality
  • Maintain and complete all repair documentation paperwork
  • Provide Level 2 support via phone to customers and internal employees
  • Abide by company safety and health policies
  • Low voltage electrical repair, using Multimeter, Oscilloscope, and other hand tools to troubleshoot and repair equipment
  • Set appointments to perform preventive maintenance, service calls, and installations
  • Work closely with the Client Relations team to resolve customer issues
  • Perform device calibration using specified test equipment such as power meters

  • Develop troubleshooting documents for our Client Relations team

  • Planning
  • Problem Solving/Analysis
  • Technical Capacity
  • Organizational Skills
  • Customer Facing Communication Proficiency
  • Ability to retain large amounts of information

  • Ability to read diagrams and schematics
  • Microsoft Applications (MS Office, Excel, Visio, PowerPoint, and Outlook)

  • Positive attitude and approach to the job responsibilities and the Alma team
  • Ability to multitask

This position has no direct reports but assists in mentoring peers and other departments as needed.

Work Environment

This job operates in a professional office environment as well as medical offices in the field. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets and fax machines. This position also utilizes hand tools and electrical meters.

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. The employee is occasionally required to sit; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 70 pounds.   • Own score reproducibility across scanners, institutions, staining protocols, and patient populations.

  • Develop and integrate mechanistic interpretability methods to explain model decisions, build clinician trust, and drive actionable model improvements.

  • Mentor and coach machine-learning scientists and engineers, fostering their technical growth and collaboration skills, and raise the bar on scientific rigor, code quality, and written communication across the team.

Experience Requirements:

  • 5+ years of industry experience building deep learning systems in PyTorch (or TensorFlow).

  • 2+ years of experience as a technical lead, launching and monitoring machine-learning products in production environments.

  • Proven ability to communicate complex ML concepts effectively to cross-functional, non-ML collaborators.

  • Experience with cloud-scale training and workflow orchestration (e.g., Flyte / Union, Kubernetes, AWS), experiment tracking, and reproducible ML pipelines.

You'll take initiatives that start as a paragraph and a target quarter, break them into a plan people can act on, and keep a distributed group of teams moving in the same direction until it's out the door. This role is for someone energized rather than frustrated by ambiguity — you'll frequently be the person who turns "we're doing this next quarter" into a sequenced plan with owners and dates, and then holds everyone to it.

You’ll also have opportunities to contribute to other initiatives that directly advance our core values and support you in elevating your craft.

How You’ll Contribute

In this role, you will have the opportunity to

  • Own the end-to-end plan for assigned initiatives — scope, sequence, dependencies, milestones, and readiness criteria from commitment through release.

  • Break large, ambiguous initiatives into discrete workstreams with clear owners, and keep the group aligned as things shift.

  • Work alongside Product Managers and Engineering Leads to track delivery against commitments, surface slippage early, and keep cross-team dependencies visible and resolved.

  • Facilitate the sessions that move work forward — dependency reviews, cross-team planning, release readiness — and make sure they end in decisions.

  • Translate engineering blockers and technical trade-offs into clear, honest updates for Product leadership and commercial stakeholders.

  • Drive go-to-market readiness with Product Marketing, Sales Enablement, Support, and Customer Success so enablement lands with the release, not after it.

  • Coordinate internal and customer-facing release communications, including release notes.

  • Build the templates, checklists, and repeatable processes that make the next release easier than the last one — using AI tooling to cut the manual overhead.

What Success Looks Like

  • Within 3 months: You've built working relationships across Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Support, and you own end-to-end coordination for two or more active initiatives — running the delivery cadence with the dev teams and producing status reporting people actually read.

  • Within 6 months: You're anticipating blockers rather than reporting them, and releases you coordinate go out with GTM readiness in place on day one.

  • Within 1 year: You run our most complex, multi-team initiatives with minimal oversight, and the delivery and launch process you've built is what the rest of the team uses by default.

  • Your legacy: Panopto ships predictably, and every team knows what's coming and what they need to do about it — because you built the system that makes that true.

Values in Action

  • Customer First, Always: You proactively surface friction points in the customer experience before they are escalated — and propose solutions, not just reports.

  • Thrive Together: You share work-in-progress for early feedback, knowing that challenge improves the outcome. You separate critiques of ideas from critiques of people.

  • Elevate the Craft: You hold the bar high on your own work and invest in developing those around you. You treat every project as an opportunity to learn something new.

  • Act with Ownership: You define success by outcomes, not activity. You flag problems early and bring a proposed path forward, not just the problem.

  • Clarity Over Complexity: You default to the simpler solution. Your written communication — internal or external — is direct, specific, and free of filler.

How We Thrive

You'll join a team where we challenge ideas, not people. The Product organization exists to ideate, define, and deliver best-in-class products to our customers — assessing market trends, running competitive and customer research, and ruthlessly prioritizing the opportunities with the highest return. We hold ourselves accountable to outcomes, not activity.

The Foundation for Success

  • 6+ years of project or program management experience, with at least 4+ years specifically embedded within a B2B SaaS Product or R&D organization.

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience.

  • Demonstrated experience running delivery with software engineering teams and coordinating the go-to-market side of a product launch. This role does both.

  • Proven experience driving delivery for complex SaaS architectures (e.g., API integrations, multi-tenant cloud platforms, feature flags, continuous deployment release models).

  • Working understanding of the SaaS product lifecycle and agile delivery practices, with the judgment to adapt the process to the situation rather than apply it by the book.

  • Enough technical fluency to hold a credible conversation with engineers about dependencies, trade-offs, and blockers — you don't need to write code, but you can't be a passenger in the discussion.

  • Proficiency with Jira and Confluence for planning, tracking, and documentation.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to push back constructively on scope creep.

  • Experience working with distributed teams across multiple time zones.

  • Demonstrated track record of designing, implementing, or improving cross-functional delivery and GTM release frameworks, rather than just executing within existing ones.

What Sets You Apart

  • Experience coordinating GTM launch activities with Product Marketing, Sales Enablement, or Customer Success.

  • Experience presenting, reporting delivery health, and managing trade-offs directly with VP and C-level stakeholders.

  • Experience sitting inside a Product or R&D organization rather than a central PMO.

  • Active PMP, PMI-ACP, or CSM certification.

  • Hands-on experience leveraging modern PM stacks (Jira, Confluence) and AI productivity tools to streamline status reporting, documentation, and risk analysis.

  • Prior experience in a Product Operations (ProdOps) function.

  • Familiarity with API-based products, feature flagging, or cloud service constraints.

  • Experience in EdTech or with higher education or enterprise customers.

  • Practical use of AI tooling to accelerate planning, synthesis, and reporting work.

Join Us

Join Panopto and play a key role in shaping the security foundation of a platform used by millions. If you love threat modeling, automating defenses, guiding engineering teams, and turning compliance standards into practical, scalable security practices, you’ll feel right at home here.

Total Rewards

Base pay offered may vary depending on various factors, including, but not limited to: job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and other eligibility factors such as geographic location. The Total Rewards package includes competitive base pay and an opportunity to enroll in a variety of benefit programs such as health insurance, flexible spending accounts, retirement savings plans, life and disability insurance programs, and programs that provide for both paid and unpaid time away from work. At Panopto, we know that great people make an organization great. We value our people and offer employees benefits that are market competitive for our industry. Learn more about what working at Panopto can mean for you.

At Panopto, our commitment to pay equity and transparency is unwavering. We do not engage in salary negotiations beyond the established range to maintain fairness and prevent potential pay disparities among team members based on negotiation strategies.

Please note: Compensation: For U.S.-based hires, the expected annual base salary range for this position is $138,000 - $148,000 USD. Actual compensation will depend on factors including skills, experience, location, and market data.

For candidates hired outside the United States, compensation will be determined using local market benchmarks and will be paid in the applicable local currency. Total compensation and benefits may vary by country.

Beyond the Requirements: At this point, we hope you're feeling excited about the job description you’re reading. Even if you don't feel that you meet every single requirement, we still encourage you to apply. We're eager to meet people that believe in our mission and can contribute to our team in a variety of ways - not just candidates who check all the boxes. Our people and culture

Panopto’s mission is to be the leader in visual and audio-based learning in a capture and post-capture world. Our user base is as diverse as the world’s universities and businesses. Panopto’s commitment to fostering a fair, equitable, and inclusive culture empowers each member of our team to express their authentic selves, contribute their distinct perspectives and make a meaningful impact both individually and collectively. This inclusive environment not only encourages creativity and the free exchange of ideas but also harnesses the power of varied viewpoints. As a result, we are better equipped to tackle our most intricate challenges, leveraging the wealth of different experiences and backgrounds within our team. This collaborative spirit empowers us to challenge ideas (not people) recognizing that our shared success relies on collective wisdom. It drives us to continuously improve and innovate, ultimately elevating the quality of our products and services. It’s what sets Panopto apart as a unique and rewarding place to work.

Our purpose

We believe that video can have a transformative effect on learning. So we built a video knowledge management platform that helps businesses and universities improve the way that they train, teach, and share knowledge. Since 2007, we have been a pioneer in video capture software, video management, and inside-video-search technology. Panopto has been adopted by more than 1,600 companies and universities worldwide with over 11 million end users. Today, Panopto’s knowledge management platform is the largest repository of expert learning videos in the world. A proud remote-first company, Panopto is headquartered in Pittsburgh, with offices in London, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Sydney, and has received industry recognition for its innovation, rapid growth, and company culture.

Panopto is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

We value and encourage diversity and solicit applications from all qualified individuals which will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability or protected veteran status, or any other legally protected criteria, in accordance with applicable law. Job Applicant Privacy Notice (compliant with GDPR)

As part of any recruitment process, Panopto collects and processes personal data relating to job applicants. The organization is committed to being transparent about how it collects and uses that data and to meeting its data protection obligations.

What information do we collect?

·Panopto collects a range of information about you. This includes:

·your name, address and contact details, including email address and telephone number;

·details of your qualifications, skills, experience and employment history;

·information about your current level of remuneration, including benefit entitlements;

·whether or not you have a disability for which the organization needs to make reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process; and

·information about your entitlement to work in the UK.

Panopto may collect this information in a variety of ways. For example, data might be contained in application forms, CVs or resumes, obtained from your passport or other identity documents, or collected through interviews or other forms of assessment. We may also collect personal data about you from third parties, such as references supplied by former employers. We will seek information from third parties only once a job offer to you has been made and will inform you that we are doing so. Data will be stored in a range of different places, including on your application record, in HR management systems and on other IT systems (including email).

Why does Panopto process personal data?

We need to process data to take steps at your request prior to entering into a contract with you. We may also need to process your data to enter into a contract with you. In some cases, we need to process data to ensure that we are complying with its legal obligations. For example, it is mandatory to check a successful applicant's eligibility to work in the UK before employment starts.

Panopto has a legitimate interest in processing personal data during the recruitment process and for keeping records of the process. Processing data from job applicants allows us to manage the recruitment process, assess and confirm a candidate's suitability for employment and decide to whom to offer a job. We may also need to process data from job applicants to respond to and defend against legal claims. Panopto may process special categories of data, such as information about ethnic origin, sexual orientation or religion or belief, to monitor recruitment statistics. We may also collect information about whether or not applicants are disabled to make reasonable adjustments for candidates who have a disability. We process such information to carry out its obligations and exercise specific rights in relation to employment.

If your application is unsuccessful, Panopto may keep your personal data on file in case there are future employment opportunities for which you may be suited. We will ask for your consent before it keeps your data for this purpose and you are free to withdraw your consent at any time.

Who has access to data?

Your information may be shared internally for the purposes of the recruitment exercise. This includes members of the HR and recruitment team, interviewers involved in the recruitment process, managers in the business area with a vacancy and IT staff if access to the data is necessary for the performance of their roles.

We will not share your data with third parties, unless your application for employment is successful and we make you an offer of employment. We will then share your data with former employers to obtain references for you, employment background check providers to obtain necessary background checks.

How does Panopto protect data?

We take the security of your data seriously. We have internal policies and controls in place to ensure that your data is not lost, accidentally destroyed, misused or disclosed, and is not accessed except by our employees in the proper performance of their duties.

For how long does Panopto keep data?

If your application for employment is unsuccessful, the organization will hold your data on file for 6 (six) months after the end of the relevant recruitment process. If you agree to allow us to keep your personal data on file, we will hold your data on file for a further 6 (six) months for consideration for future employment opportunities. At the end of that period, or once you withdraw your consent, your data is deleted or destroyed. You will be asked when you submit your CV whether you give us consent to hold your details for the full 12 months in order to be considered for other positions or not.

If your application for employment is successful, personal data gathered during the recruitment process will be transferred to your Human Resources file (electronic and paper based) and retained during your employment. The periods for which your data will be held will be provided to you in a new privacy notice.

Your rights

As a data subject, you have a number of rights. You can:

·access and obtain a copy of your data on request;

·require the organization to change incorrect or incomplete data;

·require the organization to delete or stop processing your data, for example where the data is no longer necessary for the purposes of processing; and

·object to the processing of your data where Panopto is relying on its legitimate interests as the legal ground for processing.

If you would like to exercise any of these rights, please contact . If you believe that the organization has not complied with your data protection rights, you can complain to the Information Commissioner.

What if you do not provide personal data?

You are under no statutory or contractual obligation to provide data to Panopto during the recruitment process. However, if you do not provide the information, we may not be able to process your application properly or at all.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Panopto AI Use Policy:

Panopto’s AI Use Policy is committed to a hiring process that is thoughtful, fair, and centered on human connection. As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more prevalent in the workplace, we believe that it is important to describe our use of AI in the hiring process, as well as outline to candidates what use of AI is and is not allowed. While AI can be a valuable tool, it cannot replace genuine human interaction or an individual’s unique perspective, experience, and voice.

Company Use of AI:

Panopto may utilize tools to enhance the efficiency, objectivity, and quality of our recruitment and evaluation process. These tools assist our team throughout the hiring lifecycle by focusing on four key areas:

  • Content Creation: Providing a starting point for crafting job descriptions and assisting in building tailored interview questions.

  • Resume Parsing: Analyzing candidate skillsets and resume alignment to efficiently identify qualified candidates.

  • Interview & Assessment Insights: Providing interview transcription, summarization, and identifying key insights from candidate assessments in relation to specific role requirements.

  • Data Organization: Organizing and storing information gathered during assessments to help our team make informed, data-driven decisions.

Ultimately, these tools are used to support—not replace—our team in assessing skills, generating insights, and identifying the best talent for Panopto.

To ensure fairness and transparency:

Human-Centric Decisions: Please be assured that AI tools are used to support our team, and all final hiring decisions are made by human reviewers. Panopto hiring teams will thoroughly review your application and assessment results. AI is not used to make final decisions regarding your candidacy.

Bias Mitigation: We are committed to algorithmic fairness. Our AI-assisted tools undergo regular independent audits to detect and mitigate bias, with the goal of keeping our processes equitable and inclusive. Our methodology aligns with global best practices and regional digital ethics standards to provide every candidate with a fair and merit-based evaluation.

Your Rights & Accommodations: We provide inclusive access for all applicants. If you require a reasonable adjustment due to a disability, or if you prefer a non-automated review of your application, please contact Panopto Talent Attraction. We respect your right to request human intervention; please note that opting for a manual review may impact the standard processing timeline.

Data Privacy and Security:

Your personal data and recordings are processed securely in compliance with global privacy and employment regulations (including EEOC, GDPR, and other local or regional privacy laws, as applicable).

To facilitate our recruitment and evaluation process, limited candidate data may be shared securely with trusted third-party vendors and service providers acting on our behalf. We retain candidate data only as long as necessary to fulfill the recruitment purpose or as required by applicable statutory retention periods. Once this purpose is met, or the retention period expires, your data is securely deleted or anonymized in accordance with our data governance policy.

Panopto is dedicated to a fair and equitable hiring process for all candidates.

Use of AI:

Statement of Transparency:

At Panopto, we embrace the transformative power of AI to enhance productivity and learning. We believe in providing a level playing field where candidates can use modern tools to put their best foot forward, provided those tools support, rather than replace, their authentic voice and expertise. While we encourage the use of AI as a tool for growth and preparation, we require transparency and authenticity to ensure a fair evaluation for all.

Acceptable Use:

  • AI-Assisted Preparation: You are encouraged to use Generative AI (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini) as a mock interviewer or coach to refine your speaking points.

  • Research & Knowledge Gathering: Using AI to synthesize industry trends or company background is permitted and viewed as proactive preparation.

  • Career Guidance Tools: Simulation tools that help you practice the STAR method or identify skill gaps are acceptable.

Prohibited Use:

  • Live Interview Assistance: The use of real-time AI "teleprompters," live answer-generators, or deepfake audio/video during Panopto recordings or live sessions is strictly prohibited.

  • Plagiarized Work Samples: Any take-home assignments or portfolios must be your original work. While AI can assist in formatting or brainstorming, the core logic and execution must be yours.

Panopto has a zero-tolerance policy toward the misrepresentation of job-related skills. Consequences of using prohibited tools may result in my immediate disqualification from the hiring process, the withdrawal of any pending offer, or termination of employment if discovered after hire.

Verification of Experience:

To ensure the integrity of our hiring process and validate the skills demonstrated during your Panopto submission, Panopto may require the following "Proof of Experience":

  • Work Samples & Portfolios: Candidates may be asked to provide original work samples (e.g., code repositories, design portfolios, case studies) that pre-date the current application.

  • Digital Footprint & Professional Links: We may request links to professional profiles (e.g., LinkedIn, GitHub, Behance) to verify career trajectory and industry contributions.

Disclosures:

  • Live Validation: Any technical skill demonstrated in an asynchronous Panopto recording is subject to a live, "Human-in-the-Loop" technical assessment or deep-dive discussion.

  • Fraud Detection: Please be aware that we utilize metadata analysis and fraud detection tools to ensure the authenticity of all video submissions.

By submitting your application and participating in the recruitment process, you acknowledge and consent to Panopto's use of AI, as well as the acceptable and prohibited uses of AI as a candidate, as described above.

Panopto is dedicated to a fair and equitable hiring process for all candidates.

Partners use Pass It Back, an integrated suite of rugby and life-skills learning products, to support children and young people in vulnerable situations to develop critical social and emotional skills. These capabilities better equip participants to navigate challenges, contribute positively to their communities, and take on leadership roles in their lives.

ChildFund Rugby is World Rugby’s global Social Impact Partner, a multi-year partnership that builds on previous partnerships across five consecutive Rugby World Cup events.

ChildFund Rugby is led by ChildFund Australia on behalf of the ChildFund Alliance, a global network of 11 organisations which assists almost 36 million children and their families in 66 countries.

ChildFund Rugby's work includes supporting rugby organisations and partners to strengthen safeguarding in sport, translating safeguarding policies, frameworks and commitments into practical systems and behaviours.

Purpose

The purpose of this Consultancy is to provide Safeguarding in Sport Facilitation services to support ChildFund Rugby's safeguarding partnerships and initiatives.

The Consultant will:

  • Facilitate high-quality, participatory safeguarding learning with rugby organisations and stakeholders.
  • Support participants to translate safeguarding frameworks and principles into practical organisational action.
  • Facilitate sensitive safeguarding discussions in a safe, respectful and appropriate manner.
  • Support implementation planning and follow-up with participating organisations.
  • Work within ChildFund Rugby's agreed safeguarding methodology, materials and facilitator boundaries.
  • Contribute to safeguarding delivery in English and/or French, according to the Consultant's language capabilities and assigned activities.

The Consultant's initial assignment will support delivery of the CAP Safeguarding Initiative with Rugby Africa Member Unions. Additional ChildFund Rugby safeguarding facilitation assignments may be agreed separately according to need, experience and availability.

Scope of Services

1. Facilitator Preparation and Training

The Consultant will complete ChildFund Rugby facilitator preparation before undertaking safeguarding delivery.

This will include:

  • Familiarising themselves with the safeguarding frameworks, policies, procedures and resources relevant to each assignment.
  • Reviewing assigned facilitation guides, presentations and implementation tools.
  • Understanding the objectives and methodology of activities they will facilitate.
  • Participating in practice facilitation and scenario discussions where required.
  • Understanding facilitator boundaries, including when safeguarding or technical questions must be escalated rather than answered without certainty.
  • Coordinating roles and responsibilities with other facilitators before delivery.

For the CAP Safeguarding Initiative, this will include specific preparation on the Rugby Africa Safeguarding Policy, Procedures and Toolkit and the agreed CAP facilitation materials.

Deliverable: Completion of required facilitator preparation and readiness for assigned safeguarding delivery.

2. Safeguarding Learning Facilitation

The Consultant will support or lead assigned safeguarding learning sessions using agreed ChildFund Rugby and partner materials.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Facilitating assigned activities, discussions and scenarios.
  • Supporting participants to understand and navigate relevant safeguarding frameworks and resources.
  • Helping participants apply safeguarding principles to their own organisational and sporting context.
  • Leading or supporting breakout discussions.
  • Encouraging participation and shared problem-solving.
  • Supporting participants to identify realistic safeguarding actions and priorities.
  • Monitoring questions and identifying areas requiring clarification or technical follow-up.
  • Ensuring quieter participants have opportunities to contribute.
  • Managing sensitive discussions appropriately and maintaining a respectful learning environment.
  • Working collaboratively with other members of the facilitation team.

For the CAP Safeguarding Initiative, English-language sessions will normally be led by the ChildFund Rugby Lead Facilitator, with Consultants supporting assigned components of delivery.

French-language facilitators will work as a facilitation team to deliver the agreed sessions in French, with lead and supporting responsibilities agreed before each session.

Deliverable: Delivery of assigned safeguarding learning sessions in accordance with agreed facilitation materials and methodology.

3. Implementation and Follow-Up Support

The Consultant may be assigned to support participating organisations following facilitated learning sessions.

This may include:

  • Reviewing progress against safeguarding action plans.
  • Supporting organisations to review or refine safeguarding reporting arrangements.
  • Reviewing safeguarding risk assessments, service maps or other implementation outputs.
  • Discussing implementation barriers and practical solutions.
  • Clarifying the use of relevant safeguarding resources.
  • Helping organisations identify realistic next steps.
  • Identifying areas requiring additional technical support.

Facilitators assigned to an organisation during learning sessions may also be assigned to support that organisation during follow-up, providing continuity across learning and implementation support.

For CAP, this may include individual calls with participating Rugby Africa Member Unions to review their Safeguarding Action Plan, Safeguarding Community Service Map and other agreed implementation priorities.

Deliverable: Completion of assigned implementation support calls and concise documentation of progress, actions and matters requiring follow-up.

4. Safeguarding Facilitation Responsibilities

Across all assignments, the Consultant will:

  • Create a respectful and psychologically safe learning environment.
  • Avoid requesting unnecessary details of identifiable safeguarding cases during learning activities.
  • Never promise complete confidentiality where an actual safeguarding concern is disclosed.
  • Follow the appropriate safeguarding reporting procedure where information suggests someone may currently be at risk.
  • Maintain appropriate confidentiality regarding participant and organisational discussions.
  • Not investigate safeguarding concerns.
  • Not provide legal, investigative, counselling or specialist advice outside their role or expertise.
  • Use agreed escalation processes where technical questions cannot confidently be answered.
  • Promptly raise significant safeguarding concerns or uncertainties with the designated ChildFund Rugby safeguarding or technical lead.
  • Use relevant agreed safeguarding resources as the primary technical reference point.

The Consultant's role is to facilitate safeguarding learning and implementation. It is not to act as an investigator, counsellor, legal adviser or statutory safeguarding authority.

5. Documentation and Debrief

Following assigned activities, the Consultant may be required to provide concise information including:

  • Participation information.
  • Key implementation issues or challenges identified.
  • Questions requiring technical follow-up.
  • Agreed organisational actions or priorities.
  • Relevant information required for subsequent implementation support.
  • Any safeguarding concern requiring escalation through the appropriate procedure.

Identifiable safeguarding information must only be recorded or shared in accordance with applicable safeguarding procedures.

Deliverable: Required session documentation and participation in short facilitator debriefs where requested.

Management and Reporting Arrangements

The Consultant will report to the ChildFund Rugby Training Experience Coordinator for assigned facilitation activities.

Specific assignments, delivery dates, language requirements and facilitation responsibilities will be agreed as part of delivery planning.

The Consultant will coordinate with ChildFund Rugby and other facilitators before delivery, advise as early as possible if unable to fulfil an agreed assignment, and raise technical or safeguarding questions promptly.

Confidentiality

All discussions and documents relating to this ToR will be treated as confidential by the parties.

Requirements

The Consultant will be required to comply with and sign a Code of Conduct that outlines safeguarding and prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment obligations.

Child Safeguarding

The successful applicant will be required to comply with and sign a Code of Conduct. The Consultant will also be required to have in place relevant background and/or criminal checks.

Counter-Terrorism

ChildFund acknowledges its obligation under Australian laws relating to counter-terrorism. In order to meet its obligation, the Service Provider will be reviewed against the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) and National Security Australia lists at the onset of any financial relationship.

Code of Conduct

The Consultant will be required to comply with and sign a Code of Conduct that outlines safeguarding and prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment obligations, ethical labour standards and modern slavery prevention expectations. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in the termination of the engagement.

Acknowledgement and Disclaimer

ChildFund, its Board, and staff make no express or implied representation or warranty as to the currency, reliability, or completeness of the information contained in this ToR. Nothing in this ToR should be construed to give rise to any contractual obligations or rights, expressed or implied, by the issue of this ToR. No contract would be created until a formal written contract is executed between ChildFund and a selected Consultant.

Provider Requirements

Qualifications & Experience

  • Experience facilitating learning, workshops or group discussions.
  • Experience working with participants from different organisational and cultural contexts.
  • Experience supporting participatory learning and practical implementation.
  • Fluent working ability in English and/or French according to assigned delivery.
  • Willingness and availability to complete ChildFund Rugby safeguarding facilitator preparation and training.
  • Previous safeguarding, child protection or safe sport experience is highly desirable.
  • Experience within rugby or another sport environment is desirable.
  • Experience working with National Federations, Unions or sports governance organisations is desirable.
  • Experience facilitating virtually is desirable.

Skills

  • Strong facilitation, communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to facilitate sensitive discussions safely and respectfully.
  • Ability to ask questions and support participants to develop practical solutions rather than simply providing answers.
  • Ability to work collaboratively as part of a facilitation team.
  • Ability to recognise the boundaries of the facilitator role and escalate technical or safeguarding matters appropriately.
  • Ability to adapt facilitation to different organisational and cultural contexts.
  • Strong judgement, professionalism and commitment to safeguarding principles.

Intel 471 empowers enterprises, government agencies, and other organizations to win the cybersecurity war using the real-time insights about adversaries, their relationships, threat patterns, and imminent attacks relevant to their businesses. The company’s platform collects, interprets, structures, and validates human-led, automation-enhanced intelligence, which fuels our external attack surface and advanced behavioral threat hunting solutions. Customers utilize this operationalized intelligence to drive a proactive response to neutralize threats and mitigate risk. Organizations across the globe leverage Intel 471’s world-class intelligence, our trusted practitioner engagement and enablement, and globally-dispersed ground expertise as their frontline guardian against the ever-evolving landscape of cyber threats to fight the adversary - and win.

The Role:

Intel 471 is looking for a PHP Engineer to help maintain and modernize Atlas, an internal application our analysts use to author and publish intelligence content. Reporting to the Director of Engineering, the role is fully remote and open to candidates across Europe on a B2B 12 month contract basis.

Atlas is a mature application, and we're looking for a pragmatic engineer to help it evolve and to support its modernization onto our cloud platform. This is a hands-on role with real autonomy: you'll work on a system used across the company and help shape where it goes next. It suits a full-stack-minded engineer comfortable across an established Laravel codebase and its front-end, improving it methodically, and who values doing careful, dependable work.

Atlas is a mature Laravel application (PHP 8, MySQL) with a JavaScript, CSS and HTML front-end.

Key Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Work across the Atlas stack, the PHP/Laravel back end and its JavaScript/CSS/HTML front-end, building and maintaining features in production.
  • Keep dependencies and the framework current, and improve testing, observability and developer tooling.
  • Triage and resolve production incidents and defects.
  • Extend automated tests, CI and deployment automation so changes ship smoothly.
  • Help modernize Atlas onto our cloud platform, in coordination with the platform and DevOps teams.
  • Document the system's behaviour, dependencies and runbooks so knowledge is shared.
  • Provide regular status updates so priorities stay clear.

Education, Experience & Qualifications:

Essential

  • Demonstrable, significant professional experience building and maintaining production PHP systems.
  • Hands-on experience with the Laravel framework, including safe version and dependency upgrades.
  • Working knowledge of front-end fundamentals (JavaScript, CSS, HTML) to build and maintain Atlas's interface.
  • A track record of improving established codebases safely, evolving them rather than rewriting from scratch.
  • Strong debugging, incident-response and root-cause analysis skills.
  • Solid working knowledge of relational databases and SQL.
  • Fluency with Git and CI/CD, and disciplined testing practices.
  • Able to work autonomously and take responsibility for the work you pick up, backed by the platform and DevOps teams.
  • Professional written and spoken English (B2 or above) for effective work in a distributed team.

Desirable

  • Experience migrating or modernizing established systems.
  • Familiarity with message queues (Kafka), object storage (e.g., S3), containers (Docker/Kubernetes) and AWS.
  • Security-hardening and dependency-management experience.
  • Exposure to cyber threat intelligence, data pipelines or high-volume ingestion systems.
  • React experience, opening up contributions to our Verity platform.
  • Comfort working with AI coding assistants such as Claude or Codex.

The role reports to our Director of Engineering but will be expected to interact and work closely with other areas of the company as needed - in particular the platform and DevOps teams. It is fully remote within Europe and involves occasional travel. The role requires regular contact with our international team located in the United States, South America, Western and Eastern Europe, and Asia, so a comfort working with diverse professional and cultural backgrounds is required.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Remote-friendly culture
  • Wellness programs
  • Employee recognition program
  • A variety of professional development opportunities
  • Inclusive culture focused on people, customers and innovation

Our Culture:

The Intel 471 team is constantly growing and is always on the lookout for talented professionals who seek to operate on the forefront of the fight against threat actors impacting our customers and partners. Our culture of humility and quiet professionalism is a core attribute of Intel 471 and everyone within it. Our culture is collaborative, supportive and fast-paced. We're a mission-driven company. We're looking for talented, 'can-do' minded people with a passion for always doing the right thing.

We believe in supporting a progressive culture that allows all our people to be themselves, enjoy exciting opportunities and grow with us. That's why our culture is founded on our core values of openness, inclusion, integrity and client focus, which set the tone for how we work together and treat each other in order to empower us all – and foster a unique team spirit. View our Culture Guide to find out more about us and what it’s like to work for Intel 471!

jobs.title: Sr. UX Writer
jobs.excerpt: Who we areJellyvision makes ALEX®, the employee decision-support platform trusted by thousands of employers and millions of people to make smart benefits choices.
jobs.description:
Who we are

Jellyvision makes ALEX®, the employee decision-support platform trusted by thousands of employers and millions of people to make smart benefits choices. We’ve done that profitably, at scale, for a long time—over $600M in lifetime sales, without losing our soul or our sense of humor.

Now we’re taking on an even messier problem: Medicare.

A small, senior team is building MyALEXHealth™, a digital Medicare guide designed to help people move from employer coverage into Medicare with clarity, confidence, and dignity. Our goal is simple and ambitious: reduce decision stress, improve plan fit, and help people feel good—not overwhelmed—about one of the most important health and financial decisions they’ll ever make.

This is an incubation-stage product. Translation: ambiguity is a feature, not a bug.

What’s the role?

We need someone who can write the way people actually talk (warm, clever, human), about Medicare (a subject that fights back), inside strict federal compliance (poetry with your hands tied), while architecting the branching logic beneath the words, coaxing an AI voice into sounding like someone you'd trust, and steering the whole thing through carrier and CMS review without a single detail slipping.

If that list made you tired, we understand. If it made you a little excited, keep reading.

You are, first and last, a great writer. Everything else serves that.

Quick gut check on the voice we're after: someone decided the Part D coverage gap should be called "the donut hole," so a hole in your drug coverage would sound like a pastry. That move, making the scary thing feel like an inside joke the two of you are in on, is the whole gig. If you already have three better nicknames for Medicare's weirder corners, we should talk.

What you’ll do to be successful

1) Write like a human being

  • Draft interactive, branching advisor conversations that feel like a smart friend, not a robot reading a policy. Write the linear stuff too: teaser and marketing videos, articles, and UX copy down to the button label and the error state.
  • Keep voice and tone consistent so product and marketing read as one brand.

The bar: people forget they're being walked through Medicare and just feel helped.

2) Structure the branching and conditional logic so it's followable, buildable, and testable

  • Hand engineers requirements, not riddles: here's the script, and here's what it needs the system to do.
  • Understand how data comes back from APIs and write so the words hold up against the real, messy data, not just the happy path.

The bar: fewer "wait, the logic doesn't work that way" moments after handoff.

3) Direct the sound

  • Generate and shape AI voiceover for our host so it sounds like a person, not a GPS.
  • Direct live VO talent when a project calls for it, and pick the takes that land.
  • Edit, mix, and caption to a clean, launch-ready standard. We'll train the technical mechanics; the ear is on you.

The bar: the voice sounds real, and audio never becomes the bottleneck.

4) Get it live, and get it cleared

  • Own content in our CMS from first draft to live URL, and QA it against your own script.
  • Prep scripts for compliance review so they're accurate to the Medicare program and true to the letter of federal rules.
  • Work with team leadership on carrier and CMS feedback: sorting what needs a real change from what needs a clarifying reply, and making the change without killing the writing.

The bar: content clears review in few rounds, with the charm intact.

And the part that ties it all together: you own the script, then you coach it to life. Designers, engineers, and collaborators build with you, not for you. The vision and the translation come from you, and you bring people along by making them want to nail it. Think showrunner, not assembly line.

Experience & skills you’ll need

  • 5+ years of experience in a writing-led, multi-disciplinary role spanning some combination of interactive content, UX writing, conversational design, content strategy, or digital storytelling.
  • You write like people talk, and you're funny without visibly trying.
  • You think in systems. Branching logic and messy data don't scare you; they kind of delight you.
  • You have an ear. You can hear when a VO line runs a beat too long or lands a shade too chipper.
  • You sweat the details. In compliance, "close enough" is how brands get in trouble, and you catch the thing everyone else skims.
  • You treat AI as a power tool, not a threat. You know where it speeds you up and where it makes slop, and you never ship the slop.
  • You have the portfolio to prove it: real work where you made something complicated feel simple and something dry feel alive. Interactive, editorial, advertising, or education backgrounds all fit.

We'll teach you the rest: Medicare's rulebook, our in-house tools (some with zero documentation), and the audio-mixing mechanics. Bring the instincts. We'll bring the manuals.

The Details

  • Location: Remote
  • Salary Range: $115,000 - $130,000

What Jellyvision will give you

Check out our benefitshere!

Jellyvision is committed to continuous evolution and fostering a more diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone is welcomed, valued, and respected. It doesn’t matter your race, ethnicity, religion, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity/expression, country of origin, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding), criminal histories consistent with legal requirements or any other basis protected by law...we just want amazing people who are willing to grow along with us.

Although we have a Chicago-based HQ that employees are welcome to work out of whether they’re local or just visiting, this position is also eligible for work by a remote employee out of AZ, CA, CO, CT, FL, GA, IL, IN, KY, MA, MI, MN, NC, NY, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA or WI.

How to apply: write to us

We’re looking for writers so a resume alone won’t cut it for us. Skip the "why I'm a great fit" generic cover letter and submit this info instead to that section (in one document):

  1. A short sample of you. About 150 words, any format, that shows us your voice. Make us feel something, or make us laugh once.
  2. Since you're attaching your portfolio, choose two of your favorite pieces from it and write one line each on what was actually hard about them.

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Network Engineer to design, maintain, secure, and optimize enterprise network infrastructure across client environments.

This is not a helpdesk or support-only role. You’ll take ownership of network reliability, performance, and security across enterprise environments while supporting both day-to-day operations and long-term infrastructure initiatives.

Working across routing, switching, firewalls, VPNs, monitoring systems, and hybrid cloud environments, you’ll ensure network infrastructure remains stable, secure, scalable, and highly available.

If you enjoy solving complex networking challenges, improving infrastructure, and maintaining mission-critical systems, this role is for you.

Responsibilities

Network Infrastructure & Configuration

  • Configure, maintain, and optimize enterprise network infrastructure, including routers, switches, firewalls, and VPNs.
  • Implement and manage:
    • VLANs
    • QoS
    • VPN tunnels
    • Access Control Lists (ACLs)
    • Routing protocols including OSPF, BGP, and EIGRP
  • Perform firmware upgrades, patching, and infrastructure maintenance.
  • Support network expansion projects, migrations, and infrastructure upgrades.
  • Maintain reliable connectivity across multi-site and hybrid environments.

Network Monitoring & Troubleshooting

  • Monitor network health using tools such as:
    • SolarWinds
    • PRTG
    • Nagios
    • Zabbix
  • Diagnose and resolve latency, packet loss, DNS, routing, and connectivity issues.
  • Troubleshoot escalated incidents using tools such as Wireshark and TCPdump.
  • Perform root-cause analysis and implement long-term preventive solutions.
  • Participate in on-call support and respond to critical network incidents when required.

Network Security & Compliance

  • Configure and maintain firewall environments including:
    • Cisco
    • Palo Alto
    • Fortinet
    • Juniper
  • Implement network segmentation, ACLs, and security policies.
  • Support compliance initiatives related to:
    • PCI-DSS
    • HIPAA
    • SOX
    • GDPR
  • Assist with Zero Trust networking and secure remote access implementations.
  • Maintain a secure, resilient, and well-governed network infrastructure.

Performance Optimization & Reliability

  • Perform bandwidth utilization analysis and capacity planning.
  • Optimize network performance through redundancy, failover, and load balancing.
  • Maintain high-availability infrastructure across enterprise environments.
  • Identify bottlenecks and recommend scalable infrastructure improvements.
  • Support cloud networking integrations across AWS, Azure, and hybrid environments.

Documentation & Operational Governance

  • Maintain accurate network diagrams, topology maps, SOPs, and technical documentation.
  • Document infrastructure changes following structured change management processes.
  • Keep configurations, procedures, and documentation organized and audit-ready.
  • Collaborate closely with infrastructure, cloud, security, and DevOps teams on network initiatives.

What Makes You a Great Fit

  • You have a strong troubleshooting mindset and remain calm during critical incidents.
  • You proactively identify and resolve infrastructure risks.
  • You communicate technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • You maintain high standards for documentation and operational excellence.
  • You work independently while collaborating effectively within remote teams.
  • You take ownership of infrastructure reliability and long-term improvements.

    • OSPF
    • BGP
    • EIGRP
  • Experience configuring:
    • Routers
    • Switches
    • Firewalls
    • VPN environments
  • Experience with network monitoring and troubleshooting platforms.
  • Strong experience with Cisco networking environments or equivalent enterprise platforms.
  • Solid understanding of:
    • TCP/IP
    • DNS
    • DHCP
    • VLANs
    • QoS
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience with:
    • Palo Alto
    • Fortinet
    • Juniper
  • Experience supporting:
    • AWS VPCs
    • Azure VNets
    • Hybrid cloud networking
  • Familiarity with:
    • Python
    • Ansible
    • Terraform
  • Experience supporting multi-site enterprise environments.
  • Exposure to Zero Trust networking models and modern security frameworks.

What Success Looks Like

Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote opportunity, and we would be interested in applicants located in Spain, Sweden, UK, Ireland or Germany.

The Opportunity:

At Grafana Labs, we build observability tools that help users understand, respond to, and improve their systems – regardless of scale, complexity, or tech stack. We recently started a skunkworks initiative with a mission to bring observability to the rest of the business. Our goal is to make Grafana the single best place where humans and AI agents understand and act on real-time data from across the enterprise. As part of this initiative, we are building an AI-native data intelligence system that gives agents reliable, governed access to enterprise context. This system helps agents retrieve the right data, metadata, definitions, lineage, quality signals, and institutional knowledge without every agent builder having to maintain their own brittle context files. The principle is simple: the context system retrieves, agents decide, and data teams maintain the intelligence.

The new team is a mix of seasoned Grafanistas and new hires. We operate with a high degree of autonomy and ownership, both as individuals and as a team. Engineers are empowered to make decisions, move quickly, and validate ideas early – while being supported by a deeply collaborative culture that values curiosity, feedback, and cross-functional partnership.

We’re looking for a Staff-level Backend Engineer to help build the first production services for this context layer management system. You will design and ship the core backend architecture that powers ingestion, context storage, retrieval APIs, and agent-facing integrations. This is an early-stage role on a high-autonomy team, so you should be comfortable working through ambiguity, making pragmatic architectural decisions, and building systems that can evolve from internal dogfooding to production-grade SaaS. As the team matures, there’s a broad opportunity to expand or redefine this role based on impact and initiative.

What You'll Be Doing:

  • Build the core backend services: Design, implement, test, and operate the first services for context ingestion, context indexing, retrieval orchestration, API access, source configuration, and system administration.
  • Create a scalable SaaS foundation: Help define and build the architecture for a multi-tenant service, including tenant isolation, usage tracking, quotas, audit logs, background jobs, and reliable service boundaries.
  • Power agent-facing retrieval workflows: Build APIs and service interfaces that allow AI agents, MCP tools, CLIs, and internal applications to retrieve relevant context, provenance, confidence signals, and warnings.
  • Work across product and infrastructure: Partner with the team to make practical tradeoffs between fast experimentation and long-term reliability, especially as the project moves from prototype to production.
  • Operate what you build: Instrument services with metrics, logs, traces, alerts, and dashboards. Use observability tools to understand system behavior and improve reliability.
  • Contribute to technical direction: Help shape the architecture, service boundaries, storage choices, API contracts, deployment patterns, and engineering practices for a new product area.
  • Effective communication: You’ll be working in a highly dynamic and collaborative environment, so we need someone who can communicate effectively and contribute across teams.
  • Ownership and impact: Take full ownership of the AI solutions you develop, ensuring they are not only innovative but also scalable, maintainable, and aligned with real user workflows.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

  • Strong engineering skills: Solid experience building production-grade, user-facing software systems. You’re a self-starter, capable of tackling complex engineering problems and making UI design decisions with minimal supervision.
  • AI experience with a practical mindset: You’re familiar with AI technologies and frameworks, and you focus on delivering high-quality solutions that work in the real world, not just in theory.
  • Quick iteration and experimentation: You’re comfortable releasing prototypes, collecting feedback, and iterating with a pragmatic mindset.
  • Proven initiative: You take ownership and drive projects forward, pushing boundaries to find the most impactful solutions. You can deal with ambiguity and are able to define scope where things are loosely defined.
  • Collaborative attitude: You communicate effectively with your peers. You’re open to feedback, and you bring a solutions-oriented mindset to the table.
  • Experience with LLMs, prompt engineering, and building applications powered by GenAI.
  • Proven track record of delivering software that made it into production and is actively used by users.
  • Exposure to working in cloud-native environments (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure).
  • Experience using observability tools to understand and troubleshoot system behavior.

Bonus Points for:

  • Experience building or working with agent frameworks or multi‑agent workflows.
  • Experience as a data analyst or work with data platforms (e.g., Looker, Tableau, PowerBI, Snowflake, DataBricks)
  • Experience building tools for data engineering.

How we work:

We are a remote-first team that meets regularly over video and does most of our work asynchronously, in writing. We value creativity, diverse perspectives, and clear communication. Tempo is relied upon by prominent global organizations to monitor critical applications and infrastructure, and we expect everyone on the team, including our Staff engineers, to contribute ideas that make it a more reliable, more useful, and more loved product.

In Spain, the Base compensation range for this role is EUR 94,025 - EUR 112,830. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

  • 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
  • Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.
  • Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.
  • Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.
  • Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.
  • Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.
  • Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.
  • Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.
  • Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.
  • In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it.
  • Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable.
