jobs.title: Senior Manager, Payroll Operations & Accounting
jobs.excerpt: Partners for Rural Impact's (PRI)work began more than 30 years ago with a place-based partnership in Appalachian Kentucky, where we’ve shown demographics don’t have to determine destiny.
jobs.description:
Partners for Rural Impact's (PRI)work began more than 30 years ago with a place-based partnership in Appalachian Kentucky, where we’ve shown demographics don’t have to determine destiny. Today, we partner with rural leaders and allies across the country to share that work and build local partnerships that put young people on a path to economic mobility.

Position Summary

The Senior Manager, Payroll Operations & Accounting leads the organization’s full-cycle payroll function for a multi-state employee population, ensuring payroll is processed accurately, timely, and in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements. This is a hands-on payroll leadership role with direct responsibility for day-to-day execution, oversight, and continuous improvement of payroll operations.

This position requires strong expertise in payroll accounting and payroll-related expenses and benefits (PEBT). The Senior Manager must understand the operational and accounting lifecycle of payroll, from employee-level payroll transactions and system configuration.

The Senior Manager of Payroll Operations & Accounting also provides technical leadership in multi-state payroll taxation, payroll system configuration, benefits and retirement plan deductions and contributions, internal controls, and payroll-related audit activities.

Because payroll processes directly affect employees, the Senior Manager also maintains strong focus on the employee experience. The position periodically interacts directly with employees to resolve complex payroll matters and is expected to consider clarity, accessibility, timeliness, and employee impact when implementing payroll processes, controls, communications, and system changes.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each primary duty satisfactorily. The requirements of the position are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required, with regular and predictable attendance essential. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Payroll Operations and Oversight

  • Lead and maintain organizational accountability for full-cycle payroll operations for a multi-state employee population, including payroll activities performed by the organization’s third-party payroll provider
  • Maintain hands-on involvement throughout the payroll cycle, including data preparation, payroll calculations, review, processing, reconciliation, and post-payroll activities
  • Serve as the primary operational owner of the relationship with the organization’s third-party payroll provider
  • Coordinate with the payroll provider on system configuration, tax setup, integrations, testing, upgrades, and implementation of regulatory or organizational changes
  • Review earnings, deductions, taxes, benefit contributions, retirement plan contributions, garnishments, leave-related adjustments, and other payroll transactions for accuracy
  • Implement systems to calculate and process new hires, terminations, compensation changes, retroactive adjustments, supplemental payments, bonuses, unpaid leave, overpayments, and other non-routine transactions
  • Manage payroll corrections and off-cycle payments and ensure adjustments are appropriately reflected across payroll, accounting, tax, benefit, and retirement records
  • Establish and maintain payroll calendars, procedures, checklists, controls, and supporting documentation

Payroll Accounting and PEBT

  • Serve as subject matter expert for the accounting of payroll-related expenses and benefits (PEBT), ensuring payroll activity is complete, accurate, and appropriately classified
  • Reconcile wages, employer payroll taxes, employee deductions, employer benefit costs, and retirement plan contributions
  • Reconcile payroll records to benefit invoices, retirement plan funding records, tax reports, vendor reports, and other supporting documentation

Payroll Tax Administration

  • Oversee federal, state, and local payroll tax administration for a geographically dispersed workforce, including activities performed by the third-party payroll provider
  • Ensure employee work locations, tax jurisdictions, withholding elections, and applicable state and local tax requirements are accurately established and maintained
  • Review payroll tax calculations, deposits, filings, and reports for accuracy, completeness, and reasonableness
  • Monitor the payroll provider’s completion of required tax filings and deposits and ensure identified discrepancies are corrected timely
  • Research and resolve tax notices, filing discrepancies, registration issues, amendments, and other payroll tax matters in coordination with the payroll provider and taxing authorities
  • Monitor changes in payroll tax requirements and coordinate necessary payroll system and process changes
  • Lead payroll year-end activities, including W-2 reconciliation, taxable fringe benefit reporting, and other required adjustments

Benefits and Retirement Plan Payroll Administration

  • Oversee the payroll administration and accounting of employee benefit deductions and employer contributions
  • Ensure benefit deductions and contributions are accurately configured, calculated, withheld, funded, and recorded
  • Reconcile payroll activity to benefit enrollment records, carrier invoices, and retirement plan records
  • Oversee payroll-related retirement plan activity, including employee deferrals, employer contributions, funding, corrections, and reconciliation
  • Partner with Human Resources, Finance/Accounting, payroll and benefit vendors, and retirement plan providers to investigate and resolve deduction, contribution, enrollment, and funding discrepancies

Payroll Operations and Employee Experience

  • Serve as the escalation point for complex payroll questions and issues, researching issues thoroughly and communicating resolutions clearly and professionally
  • Ensure payroll corrections and employee-impacting issues are addressed promptly, accurately, and with appropriate communication to affected employees
  • Translate complex payroll, tax, deduction, and benefit matters into clear and understandable information for employees and other stakeholders
  • Consider the employee experience when developing or modifying payroll procedures, workflows, forms, communications, and system functionality
  • Balance operational efficiency and internal control requirements with the need for payroll processes to be understandable, accessible, and practical for employees
  • Anticipate the employee impact of payroll system or process changes and partner with Human Resources to develop appropriate communication, guidance, and implementation strategies
  • Handle employee payroll concerns with discretion, responsiveness, and sensitivity while maintaining consistent application of organizational policies and payroll requirements
  • Other roles/duties will be assigned as necessary to assist and support in the attainment of our mission

Position Location & Schedule

This position is designated as a remote/home-office position and will support an employee population primarily located across the Eastern and Central time zones. The standard work schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET.

Remote work must be performed from a location approved by PRI and in accordance with PRI's Remote Work Policy. Not all positions are eligible for remote work; eligibility is determined based on the responsibilities and operational needs of each position. Remote/home-office positions may also be subject to residency restrictions and limited to states in which PRI is authorized to employ staff.

PRI Headquarters are located in Berea, Kentucky. Occasional travel for meetings, conferences, training, or other organizational events is sometimes required. Travel may be regional or national depending on business needs.

Minimum Qualifications

Education required to ensure success in this position:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or related field
  • Certified Payroll Professional (CPP) certification preferred, but not required

Experience required to ensure success in this position:

  • Minimum of 7 years of progressively responsible payroll experience, including substantial hands-on responsibility for full-cycle payroll operations
  • Demonstrated experience leading or overseeing payroll operations for a multi-state employee population
  • Strong payroll accounting expertise, including demonstrated knowledge of payroll-related expenses and benefits (PEBT) and the accounting treatment of employee and employer payroll and benefit transactions
  • Experience overseeing payroll delivered through a third-party payroll provider, including validation of provider outputs, issue resolution, and vendor accountability
  • Strong knowledge of federal, state, and local payroll tax administration, including experience overseeing tax services performed by a third-party provider
  • Experience reconciling payroll deductions and employer contributions to benefit carrier enrollment, retirement plan, and invoicing
  • Demonstrated experience with payroll system configuration, including earnings, deductions, taxes, employer contributions, benefits, and general ledger mappings
  • Experience developing and maintaining payroll internal controls, reconciliations, and auditing documentation

Special skills, knowledge and abilities:

  • Demonstrates the technical expertise necessary to independently evaluate payroll results, challenge discrepancies, and ensure issues are resolved
  • Understands the interdependencies among payroll, HRIS, benefits, retirement, timekeeping, tax, and financial systems and can identify and resolve issues across those systems
  • Recognizes payroll as both a critical operational function and an essential employee service. Considers employee impact when making decisions about payroll processes, systems, controls, and communications
  • Analytical problem-solving approach; does not solely rely on vendor or system outputs to determine accuracy. Independently analyzes data
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and demonstrated ability to analyze complex payroll data
  • High level of discretion and sound judgment in handling confidential payroll, compensation, tax, and employee information
  • Experience in non-profit, grant-funded, or similarly complex accounting environment preferred, but not required

License, certification, or registration necessary:

  • Must have access to reliable transportation
  • Successfully complete pre-employment background check

Physical requirements:

  • Ability to work in a high-energy office
  • Ability to accurately communicate and exchange information with partners, stakeholders, and/or meeting participants
  • Ability to operate standard office equipment and computer software programs
  • Ability to travel independently by car and plane both locally and nationally

Environmental conditions:

  • Work in a fast-paced setting with frequent interruptions and shifting priorities

Additional Company Information

PRI offers a wide array of benefit options, to meet the financial, educational, and health needs of you and your family.

  • Comprehensive insurance plans including medical, dental, vision, and prescription coverage.
  • Flexible spending accounts, plus an employee assistance program.
  • Life and long-term disability insurance and retirement plan.
  • Generous paid time off work options including vacation, sick leave, and annual holidays, in addition to paid parental leave.
  • Tuition assistance and professional development for employees.

Partners for Rural Impact is an Equal Opportunity Employer that recruits and hires qualified candidates without regard to race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, disability, or veteran status.

Responsibilities

I2X Technologies is a reputable technology services company to the Federal Government. I2X Technologies is seeking a Software Unit Tester

Qualifications

Qualifications:

  • Knowledge of software unit test processes required
  • 5+ years of Experience with unit test for the C or C++ languages required
  • Experience with Google test software test tool required
  • Experience with embedded flight software
  • Multiple platform experience helpful (Unix, MS Windows, Linux)

  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills required

US Citizenship is required.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee will regularly sit, walk, stand and climb stairs and steps. May require walking long distance from parking to work station. Occasionally, movement that requires twisting at the neck and/or trunk more than the average person, squatting/ stooping/kneeling, reaching above the head, and forward motion will be required. jobs.excerpt: Local Progressand Local Progress Impact Lab are seeking a full-time California Director.
jobs.description:
Local Progressand Local Progress Impact Lab are seeking a full-time California Director.

About Local Progress and Local Progress Impact Lab

Local Progress and the Local Progress Impact Lab work collectively to advance a racial and economic justice agenda through all levels of government. Local Progress (LP) is a movement of nearly 1,800 local elected officials advancing a racial and economic justice agenda through all levels of local government. The Local Progress Impact Lab (the Impact Lab) brings together local leaders, partners, and experts to build the knowledge, skills, and leadership needed to advance racial and economic justice at the local level.

About the Position:

Local Progress and the Impact Lab are seeking a California Director with a track record of organizing, base and coalition building to support our ever-growing work in California, including training and facilitation, strategic campaigning, fundraising, staff management and supervision.

Working as part of a Membership and Organizing team, the California Director will be working in deep collaboration and coordination with the current California Coordinator to strengthen the organizing infrastructure in the state. Additionally, the California Director will also be responsible for envisioning and building out our statewide strategy, which involves membership recruitment and engagement, and identifying and cultivating relationships and buy-in from key allies, organizational partners and funders. The California Director will supervise and support the development of Membership and Organizing Team members.

The ideal candidate for this job is someone with a track record of relational organizing, developing leaders, and bringing people across diverse backgrounds and opinions together in coalition to shift the material conditions of our communities. We’re looking for a strategic thinker who also pays attention to details and knows how to build systems to reduce redundancies, and increase efficiency by creating tools to produce high quality work. Other key qualifications include strong supervision, fundraising and funder cultivation experience and a keen interest in transformational policy and organizing at the municipal level.

The California Director will report to the Organizing Director.

Location: This is a remote position with no in-office requirement. However the candidate must live in California, with a preference for Northern California.

Primary Responsibilities:

Support Local Progress and the Impact Lab’s work in maintaining the California State Chapter and lead the development of a Statewide strategy:

  • Statewide Strategy: Spearhead the exploration, development and implementation of a statewide strategy, building an organizing and governance infrastructure to grow and strengthen membership, and support and mobilize local electeds across the state. Represent Local Progress, the Impact Lab, and the state chapter in statewide coalitions, campaigns, and other strategic tables. Work to embed Local Progress within the state's movement ecosystem so that it is recognized as a trusted, indispensable partner and one of the core pillars of progressive advocacy and organizing across the state.
  • Membership recruitment, organizing and support. Expand and strengthen the Local Progress California-based membership, including creating and implementing a strategy to continue to both recruit new members and increase engagement of existing members across the state. Provide and facilitate policy, communications and campaigns support to Local Progress members.
  • Partnerships & Collaborative Governance: Identify and cultivate deep, long-term relationships and buy-in from key allies, state and local partners, labor and funders in California to align on shared priorities and collaborate by establishing Local Progress as a trusted and strong coalition partner that helps strategize, launch and coordinate trans-local and statewide campaigns.
  • Leadership Development: Collaborate across Local Progress teams to plan, design, and execute robust local and statewide leadership development initiatives that equip California members to govern effectively, lead with equity, and organize for impact.

Support Local Progress and the Impact Lab’s national work:

  • Cross-team collaboration: Collaborate across Local Progress teams to support organizational activities and infrastructure including caucuses, state chapter activities, Collaborative Governance Academy, Collaborative Governance Labs, reports, convenings, web products, etc.
  • Supervision: Supervise up to 3 members of the organizing team and help develop a culture of excellent supervision and staff development within Local Progress and the Impact Lab.
  • Fundraising: Lead a fundraising portfolio with an assigned annual fundraising goal, cultivating new and maintaining existing relationships and identifying new funding opportunities.
  • Policy & Program support: Supporting national projects (policy, organizing or campaign related).

Required Qualifications

  • Must reside in California, with a preference for Northern California
  • 7-10+ years of organizing, strategic campaigning, and/or advocacy experience.
  • 3+ years of demonstrated success in supervising staff working across a breadth of issues and functions.
  • 3-5 years of demonstrated history of success in fundraising
  • Experience in relational organizing and an ability to relate to and move to action a diverse group of people from a variety of local contexts and backgrounds, including in a virtual setting.
  • A background and skill set in designing membership-based and/or issue-based organizing strategies.
  • Ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects, create and execute organizing work plans, anticipate obstacles and identify ways to navigate challenges, identify and involve stakeholders appropriately, and drive projects independently.
  • A commitment to inside/outside strategy and movement governance that features deep partnership between “outside” organizing and “inside” elected officials.
  • A demonstrated commitment to social, racial, and economic justice and a deep interest in local policy, politics, and government.
  • Ambition, drive, energy, and the ability to work flexible, long hours when necessary and travel (approximately 1-2x per month up to 6 days a month).

The Ideal Candidate will have:

  • Experience in leading and managing multi-stakeholder coalitions.
  • Previous experience working with elected officials.

Salary and Benefits:

Salary will be determined according to a salary scale which takes into account years of experience, job duties, and other factors, but is expected to be between $105,800 and $124,200.

We operate on a four day workweek with a default schedule of Monday through Thursday. We have a generous benefits package, including health insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, five weeks of vacation per year, 20 sick days per year, paid holidays, and contributions to individuals’ 403(b) plans. The Local Progress office is closed between December 24 and January 1 annually.

This is a management position and will not be part of the Local Progress bargaining unit.

Timeline:

We encourage applicants to apply by October 9, 2026, for an anticipated start date of January 19, 2027. Applicants will be screened on a rolling basis so we encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible. If you have any time constraints, please indicate as much in your application.

How to apply:

Please submit your cover letter and resume through the JazzHR portal.

Local Progress Values

  • Respect: We value people and treat each other with dignity. We strive to understand each other as full human beings, and give each other grace and room to grow.
  • Honesty: We communicate directly with each other, are honest about our strengths and our shortcomings, and are transparent about who has what level of information and authority and why.
  • Groundedness: We are authentic, and have high humility and low ego. We ground our work in the day-to-day reality and needs of our members.
  • Mutual accountability: We do what we say we're going to do, follow through on our commitments to each other and to our members, and we hold each other to a high bar. We self-reflect and develop each other’s skills as leaders.
  • Nuance: We understand that our work is complex and hold space for multiple viewpoints, contradictions, and tensions. We can hold many things as true while making decisions that advance our mission.
  • Impact: We empower our team to make decisions to drive their work. We are focused on results, persistent in overcoming obstacles, and adapt to changing external conditions. We take pride in our work.
  • Collaboration: We come together across different levels of power to advance shared interests. We center what’s best for the organization and are team players.
  • Joy: We value playfulness, humor, and joy as ways to create community, connection, and goodwill that sustains us through the challenges inherent in our work.

Local Progress is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and actively recruits people of color, womxn, individuals with disabilities, and members of the LGBTIQAA+ community.

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Client Business Hours

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Customer Success Manager (CSM) / Account Manager to own customer relationships, drive product adoption, and maximize customer retention and account growth.

This is a strategic, customer-facing role where you’ll be responsible for ensuring customers achieve measurable value from the platform while identifying opportunities to expand existing relationships.

You’ll partner closely with Sales, Product, Support, and Leadership teams to guide customers from onboarding through renewal, helping them realize long-term success and business outcomes.

If you’re passionate about customer advocacy, relationship management, and revenue retention, this role is built for you.

What You’ll Own

Customer Onboarding & Product Adoption

  • Lead customer onboarding and implementation activities.
  • Define onboarding goals, success milestones, and adoption plans.
  • Deliver onboarding sessions, product training, and customer education.
  • Accelerate customer time-to-value.
  • Monitor product usage and proactively address adoption gaps.
  • Drive long-term engagement and product utilization.

Account & Relationship Management

  • Manage a portfolio of 20–40 customer accounts.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned customers.
  • Build trusted relationships with stakeholders, decision-makers, and executive contacts.
  • Conduct:
    • Customer check-ins
    • Strategic account reviews
    • Success meetings
    • Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs)
  • Maintain strong account engagement and visibility.

Customer Retention & Success

  • Monitor customer health using platforms such as:
    • Gainsight
    • ChurnZero
    • Totango
    • Similar Customer Success tools
  • Identify:
    • Churn risks
    • Low product adoption
    • Expansion opportunities
  • Develop and execute customer success plans.
  • Ensure customers consistently achieve measurable ROI and business value.
  • Drive retention through proactive engagement.

Support Coordination & Escalation Management

  • Coordinate customer issues and internal escalations.
  • Partner closely with:
    • Support
    • Product
    • Technical teams
  • Ensure issues are resolved efficiently with clear communication.
  • Maintain customer confidence throughout the resolution process.

Renewals, Expansion & Revenue Growth

  • Own customer renewals from planning through completion.
  • Identify and drive:
    • Upsell opportunities
    • Cross-sell opportunities
    • Account expansion
  • Partner with Sales on growth initiatives.
  • Manage renewal timelines and expansion pipelines.
  • Prepare account reviews and renewal recommendations.
  • Support revenue retention and long-term customer growth.

Reporting & Customer Insights

  • Track and report on:
    • Customer health scores
    • Product usage
    • Renewal pipeline
    • Retention performance
    • Expansion opportunities
  • Gather customer feedback and advocate internally for product improvements.
  • Contribute to improving:
    • Onboarding
    • Customer experience
    • Product adoption
    • Retention programs

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • Customer-first mindset with a focus on long-term success.
  • Excellent relationship-building and communication skills.
  • Strong executive presence and presentation abilities.
  • Highly organized and proactive.
  • Comfortable balancing customer advocacy with business goals.
  • Able to manage multiple accounts while delivering an exceptional customer experience.
  • Ownership-driven with strong follow-through.

Required Experience & Skills

Experience

  • 2–3+ years of experience in:
    • Customer Success
    • Account Management
    • Client-facing SaaS
    • Customer-facing service environments
  • Proven success managing customer relationships, renewals, and account growth.

Technical & Operational Skills

  • Experience using CRM platforms such as:
    • Salesforce
    • HubSpot
    • Similar CRM systems
  • Experience with Customer Success platforms such as:
    • Gainsight
    • ChurnZero
    • Totango
  • Strong presentation and communication skills.
  • Experience leading:
    • Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs)
    • Customer training sessions
    • Strategic account discussions
  • Excellent organizational and account management skills.

Nice-to-Have

  • 3–5 years of Customer Success or Account Management experience.
  • SaaS, B2B technology, or professional services background.
  • Experience with:
    • NPS
    • CSAT
    • Customer health scoring frameworks
  • Experience creating:
    • Customer Success playbooks
    • Onboarding documentation
    • Client presentations
    • Case studies

What a Typical Day Looks Like

  • Review customer health dashboards and account activity.
  • Monitor renewal timelines and at-risk accounts.
  • Identify expansion opportunities.
  • Conduct onboarding sessions and customer success meetings.
  • Lead Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs).
  • Collaborate with Sales, Product, and Support teams.
  • Update CRM records and customer success plans.
  • Prepare recommendations to improve customer outcomes and drive account growth.

In short: You’ll help customers realize value quickly, strengthen long-term relationships, reduce churn, and drive renewals and expansion across your portfolio.

Key Metrics for Success (KPIs)

  • Net Revenue Retention (NRR)
  • Customer renewal rate
  • Expansion and upsell revenue
  • Customer health score improvements
  • Product adoption and engagement
  • NPS and CSAT scores
  • Churn reduction and customer retention

Why Join Us?

  • Own customer relationships from onboarding through renewal.
  • High-impact role directly influencing customer retention and revenue growth.
  • Collaborate closely with Sales, Product, and Leadership teams.
  • Fully remote work environment with long-term career growth.
  • Opportunity to advance into:
    • Senior Customer Success Manager
    • Strategic Account Manager
    • Customer Success Team Lead
    • Customer Success Manager
    • Revenue Operations

Interview Process

  1. Spark Hire Intro Video (3–5 minutes)
  2. Client Interview
  3. Offer & Onboarding

What Happens After You Apply

After submitting your application, you’ll receive an email invitation from Spark Hire to record a short 3–5 minute Intro Video. This is the first step in our hiring process and can be completed whenever it’s convenient for you.

Instead of multiple initial screening calls, you’ll have one opportunity to introduce yourself, discuss your Customer Success or Account Management experience, explain how you’ve onboarded customers, driven product adoption, managed renewals, or handled at-risk accounts, and share examples of how you’ve improved customer retention or expanded existing relationships. Your video will be reviewed by the hiring team before moving to the client interview.

You can record your video as many times as you’d like before submitting it—only your final version will be reviewed.

Please keep an eye on both your inbox and spam folder for your Spark Hire invitation after applying.

Apply Now

If you enjoy building lasting customer relationships, driving product adoption, and helping customers achieve meaningful business outcomes while contributing to long-term revenue growth, we’d love to hear from you. Apply today and become a trusted partner in your customers’ success.

Job Title: Medical Virtual Assistant – Hospice Intake, Insurance Verification & Billing Support [CA-T]

Position Type: Full-time
Schedule: Monday–Friday | 8:00 AM–5:00 PM MST, with a 1-hour unpaid break

Pay Rate: $5–$6 USD per hour
Location: Remote – Philippines

Client Overview & Job Summary

Our client is a U.S.-based healthcare practice seeking an experienced Medical Virtual Assistant to support patient intake, referral coordination, insurance and Medicare verification, and back-office administrative workflows.

The ideal candidate has experience supporting a hospice or similar healthcare setting, with MatrixCare experience highly preferred. The role will also assist with prior authorizations, billing and claims-related tasks, patient communication, and general administrative support.

This position is ideal for someone who is highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable taking ownership of healthcare administrative workflows from initial intake through follow-up and completion.

Key Responsibilities

Patient Intake & Referral Coordination

  • Manage inbound and outbound patient intake workflows.
  • Coordinate incoming patient referrals and accurately enter referral information into the appropriate system.
  • Collect, review, and document required new-patient intake information.
  • Follow up on missing information or documentation needed to complete referrals and intake.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient and referral records.
  • Coordinate with internal team members to ensure referrals and patient needs are addressed promptly.

Insurance & Medicare Verification

  • Verify patient insurance eligibility, benefits, and coverage.
  • Confirm valid Medicare information and primary Medicare status.
  • Identify missing, inactive, or incorrect insurance information and assist with resolving discrepancies.
  • Accurately document verification results and relevant insurance information.
  • Follow up as needed to ensure insurance requirements are completed before services are provided.

Prior Authorization & Billing Support

  • Assist with prior authorization requests, including submission, tracking, follow-up, and resolution.
  • Support medical billing and claims-related workflows.
  • Review denied claims and investigate issues such as missing authorizations, incorrect patient information, or insurance discrepancies.
  • Assist with resolving outstanding claims and claim holds.
  • Maintain accurate billing and authorization documentation.

Patient & Administrative Support

  • Provide general back-office administrative support.
  • Manage incoming and outgoing healthcare documentation and faxes as assigned.
  • Monitor and process orders and other assigned administrative tasks.
  • Provide patient phone support and respond to general inquiries.
  • Assist with scheduling requests and route patients to the appropriate team member.

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government, efficiently and effectively. jobs.description:
Ce qu’on fait chez CHASR 🎥

Ici, on est accros aux social ads sur Meta / TikTok et on a une mission : faire exploser les campagnes ads de nos clients (Sephora, Rare Beauty, Legal Place, Wecasa, IAD, Bitstack,...).

Pour ça, on ne se contente pas de balancer quelques créas dans les campagnes, prier le St Esprit de la Performance et espérer que ça marche. Non.

On teste, on analyse, on ajuste, on re-teste, jusqu’à trouver LA recette créative qui fait décoller chaque compte.

Et pour y arriver, on a plusieurs cordes à notre arc :

Stratégie créative – On scrute les comptes de nos clients sous toutes leurs coutures et on propose des recommandations créatives structurées et actionnables pour maximiser la perf'.

Copywriting – On rédige des scripts, storyboards et briefs calibrés pour scaler, jusqu’à la moindre virgule.

Production de vidéos – On produit des formats courts verticaux pensés pour la performance (UGC, VSL, contenus IA, etc.), adaptés aux codes des plateformes comme TikTok & Instagram, avec un seul objectif : capter l’attention et convertir.

Production de static ads – On crée des visuels ultra-impactants pour que même auprès d’une audience froide (glaciale !), nos créas donnent envie de cliquer.

Bref, on ne laisse rien au hasard et on met tout en œuvre pour transformer chaque euro investi.

Vos missions

Ce qu’on attend de toi 🫵

En tant que monteur vidéo freelance spécialisé UGC & VSL, tu seras un maillon clé de la performance de nos campagnes.

Tes missions incluront :

Montage UGC orienté performance

Transformer des rushs bruts (créateurs, clients, assets existants) en ads qui captent l’attention dès la première seconde et convertissent. Hook, rythme, storytelling : rien n’est laissé au hasard.

Montage VSL (Video Sales Letter)

Structurer et monter des vidéos longues ou semi-longues pensées pour vendre : narration fluide, dynamisme visuel, gestion du tempo, overlays impactants… Tu sais garder l’attention tout en maximisant la conversion.

Optimisation créative

Adapter tes montages aux codes des plateformes (TikTok, Reels, Meta Ads). Tu comprends ce qui fait performer une vidéo : pattern interrupt, pacing, sous-titres, sound design, etc.

Déclinaisons & itérations

Créer plusieurs variations à partir d’un même concept pour tester différents hooks, angles, rythmes. Chez nous, une créa = plusieurs tests.

Collaboration avec l’équipe créative

Travailler main dans la main avec les Creative Strategists pour donner vie aux concepts et scripts. Tu ne montes pas “dans ton coin” : tu contribues à la perf globale.

Vos compétences

Profil recherché 🕵️

Expérience solide en montage vidéo UGC et/ou VSL orienté performance.

Appétences pour le motion design.

Maîtrise des codes des social ads (TikTok / Meta).

Excellente compréhension du rythme, du storytelling et de la rétention.

Capacité à transformer des rushs simples en vidéos ultra engageantes et optimisées pour la conversion.

Bonne sensibilité marketing (tu comprends ce qui vend, pas juste ce qui est “beau”).

Autonomie, rapidité d’exécution et sens du détail. Pas de fautes d'orthographes ou d'erreurs de safe zones.

Ultra important : respect des deadlines !

Avantages

Ce que nous t’offrons 🎁

Un environnement de travail flexible et collaboratif, entièrement en télétravail.

Des projets variés avec des marques ambitieuses.

Un volume de créas important (tu ne vas pas t’ennuyer).

Une équipe ultra orientée performance avec laquelle tu vas progresser vite.

Une culture qui valorise la créativité, le test & learn et l’exigence.

Rémunération :

  • D’abord à la vidéo, selon tes tarifs
  • Possibilité d’évoluer vers une rémunération fixe

Pour postuler, merci de répondre au formulaire de candidature qui suit.

jobs.excerpt: OverviewHealthEdge is consolidating its Atlassian products across a post-merger portfolio of business units (GuidingCare, Wellframe, Altruista, and HealthProof/Advantasure) into a unified Cloud environment: Jira, Jira Service Management, Confluence, and Rovo/Claude.
jobs.description:
Overview

HealthEdge is consolidating its Atlassian products across a post-merger portfolio of business units (GuidingCare, Wellframe, Altruista, and HealthProof/Advantasure) into a unified Cloud environment: Jira, Jira Service Management, Confluence, and Rovo/Claude. We’re hiring a technical leader to own this consolidation end to end and the long term platform strategy: architecture, vendor management, internal product roadmap, and team leadership.

This is a hands-on role, not a pure people-management seat. You’ll set the architecture strategy your team executes against, and work with business leaders to refine strategies and define roadmaps that enable them to meet their business objectives. You’ll lead two delivery tracks — internal HealthEdge teams and external customers — through their respective managers, plus a shared platform architect function, building the in-house technical judgment we’ve relied on outside consultants for.

If you thrive on building in environments where the playbook is still being written, are excited to set a new bar for how AI changes the way a team operates, and know how to keep complex systems healthy while driving them forward, then this role is for you.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU'LL GET TO

  • Own our Atlassian architecture and governance. Set direction for our multi-instance Cloud environment, including how business units consolidate onto shared standards for permissions, SCIM/Okta identity, and Jira at scale and the tradeoff between customization and simplification.
  • Own our HIPAA/BAA compliance posture. Know BAA scope across products, Marketplace apps, integrations, and AI connectors like Rovo. Help define our go-forward strategy.
  • Own licensing strategy in partnership with procurement. Forecast demand, model tier and seat decisions against business priorities, and bring renewal recommendations forward with the numbers behind them. Procurement owns the commercial process; you own the platform judgment feeding it.
  • Partner with senior stakeholders to redesign how teams work. Go beyond standardizing tooling. Work with the business to rethink approaches to workflow and operating models as we consolidate.
  • Communicate at the executive level. Bring platform strategy and renewal decisions directly to executive level stakeholders.
  • Team building. Set the bar for ownership and delivery, reshape how the work is divided, and coach people leaders.
  • Use AI to work smarter. Bring an AI-first lens to platform design and support, for yourself and your team.
  • Deliver in increments, not big-bang. Ship in slices, prove value early, and let the roadmap adjust as you learn. Run experiments, take measured risks, and don’t let perfect block good.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • Deep, current hands-on experience with Atlassian Cloud permissions, SCIM/identity provisioning, and Jira architecture at scale.
  • Ability to read, debug, and evaluate admin tooling built against the Atlassian REST API (Python preferred).
  • A track record leading platform consolidation and workflow redesign through executive stakeholders in a post-M&A or multi-BU environment.
  • Direct, in-house platform ownership background, prioritized over pure consulting or staffing experience.
  • Experience operating a platform inside a regulated environment: HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2, PCI, FedRAMP, or GxP. You understand how compliance constrains architecture, vendor selection, and AI adoption, and you’ve navigated it without becoming a bottleneck. Healthcare specifically is a plus, not a requirement.
  • Hands-on Atlassian licensing and vendor management experience (tier modeling, seat true-ups, renewal negotiation support) is a strong plus. If you’ve owned licensing for a comparable enterprise platform instead, we’ll teach the Atlassian specifics.
  • A track record building or turning around a team: setting a high bar for performance, structuring for end to end ownership, and developing people into larger scope.
  • An iterative delivery mindset. You’ve replaced multi-quarter platform programs with shorter cycles that show value along the way, and you can point to a measured risk that didn’t pay off and what you did next.
  • AI-first and already weaving AI into how you work, and ready to set that standard for your team.

Travel%: Up to 5% for client engagements and team leadership activities

Industry: Web3 / Crypto / Infrastructure

About Vana

Vana is a layer-1 blockchain designed for user-owned data. Its mission is to build a decentralized data economy where individuals and communities can collectively own, govern, and earn from the data that powers artificial intelligence. By enabling data to exist as a new form of capital—liquid, composable, and verifiable—Vana provides the foundation for a more equitable and open AI ecosystem.

Built with privacy-preserving architecture, Vana allows users to contribute and permission data through DataDAOs—decentralized data collectives that pool user-contributed data for specific use cases, from mental health to genomics to social media. The network’s proof-of-contribution mechanism ensures that every data provider is fairly rewarded, while developers can build new data applications and liquidity pools on top of the protocol.

Following the launch of its mainnet and native token, $VANA, the network has become one of the fastest-growing ecosystems in Web3, with over a million contributors participating across hundreds of DataDAOs. As the ecosystem scales and token operations expand, Vana is seeking a Head of Finance to bring financial rigor, treasury management, and strategic discipline to a rapidly growing decentralized organization at the frontier of data and AI.

The Opportunity

This role is ideal for a technically sophisticated finance leader who combines the analytical rigour of traditional finance with a strong enough grasp of crypto market mechanics or a strong willingness to learn. The Chief Financial Officer will manage Vana’s capital strategy across fiat, token, and treasury holdings, bridging between the foundation, development company, and trading ecosystem.

You’ll advise the founders on liquidity, market structure, and macroeconomic trends impacting digital assets, while maintaining strong relationships with market makers, investors, and partners. This is a hands-on, high-trust environment that demands precision, discretion, and excellent judgment.

Key Responsibilities

1. Treasury Management

  • Determine and manage the optimal allocation between $VANA, stablecoins, and fiat reserves.

  • Design and execute treasury allocation, hedging, and yield strategies to minimize risk and preserve long-term runway.

  • Develop and implement financial mechanisms (e.g., buybacks, liquidity programs, staking strategies) that enhance network stability and sustainability.

2. Token & Asset Management

  • Manage liquidity across all exchanges where $VANA is traded, in coordination with market makers and liquid funds.

  • Oversee relationships with market makers, funds, and trading desks to ensure adequate liquidity and orderly markets.

  • Manage $VANA token and other digital asset holdings across the Foundation and affiliated entities, ensuring strategic alignment and market efficiency.

3. Financial Advisory & Tokenomics Strategy

  • Assess macroeconomic and market conditions to inform treasury allocation, liquidity management, and capital strategy.

  • Advise on internal tokenomics design, including $VANA supply schedules, on-chain liquidity, and token trading dynamics.

  • Evaluate major financial transactions, investments, and partnerships across the Foundation and development company.

  • Build financial models and scenario analyses to guide token and treasury strategy under varying market conditions.

4. Financial Management & Reporting

  • Oversee accounting, budgeting, and cashflow management across the Foundation and development company.

  • Maintain audit readiness and ensure compliance with all tax and regulatory reporting requirements.

  • Implement disciplined internal controls and a consistent financial reporting cadence.

  • Deliver accurate, timely, and actionable financial insights to support leadership decision-making.

5. Investor, Market & Partner Relations

  • Partner with the founders on fundraising, capital strategy, and investor engagement.

  • Build and manage relationships with market makers, trading desks, funds, exchanges, and other strategic partners.

  • Track and manage relationships with major $VANA token holders to support strategic ecosystem alignment.

  • Negotiate and structure liquidity, treasury, and investment deals to advance long-term financial objectives.

6. Web3 / Token-Specific Expertise (Nice to Have):

  • Deep understanding of DeFi, token liquidity management, and market-making structures.

  • Familiarity with major trading firms, funds, and counterparties across the crypto ecosystem.

  • Ability to engage intelligently in token strategy discussions to protect and advance Vana’s financial and reputational interests.

Ideal Profile

  • Background in finance, investment banking, venture capital, or corporate finance, with direct exposure to crypto, DeFi, or Web3 markets.

  • Demonstrated experience managing treasury strategy, liquidity, and investor relations in high-growth environments.

  • Strong grasp of financial instruments, trading structures, and market mechanics relevant to digital assets.

  • Deep integrity and discretion; understands incentive misalignment risks in crypto and acts with transparency and accountability.

  • High emotional intelligence and relationship fluency; capable of managing investors, market makers, and partners with credibility and composure.

  • Systems thinker who brings structure and discipline to complex, fast-moving financial ecosystems.

  • Mission-aligned: motivated by building a sustainable data economy, not by short-term financial extraction.

Additional Notes

  • The ideal candidate should be comfortable navigating the intersection of traditional finance and crypto culture.

  • Familiarity with liquidity provisioning, token flows, and KOL/MM dynamics is beneficial but not essential.

  • Strong preference for candidates who can bring discipline and trustworthiness i.e. “grown-up energy”, to a space that often lacks both.

jobs.description:
JLL empowers you to shape a brighter way.

Our people at JLL are shaping the future of real estate for a better world by combining world class services, advisory and technology for our clients. Whether you’ve got deep experience in commercial real estate, skilled trades or technology, or you’re looking to apply your relevant experience to a new industry, join our team as we help shape a brighter way forward.

JLL - BMS/OT Technology Support Specialist (P4)

Location: Anywhere in the US (ET preferred)

Work Schedule: Remote, M-F 8 AM - 5 PM

Reports to: Head of Smart Building Services, Americas

Estimated compensation for this position is: $100,600 - $137,000 annually

What this job involves:

The BMS / OT Technology Support Specialist provides hands-on technical expertise supporting building technology (BT) operations for assigned client accounts, covering the full stack of BT assets — from BMS supervisory controllers and HVAC interface devices to the compute infrastructure that supports them. This role is the primary technical executor for the account’s building technology program and works in close coordination with the Building Technology Coordinator. This role is part of the Operational Technology team, whose combined expertise covers the full technical scope below. Candidates are not expected to have deep expertise in every technical area — a highly desired candidate will have a broad knowledge of all areas with strong, demonstrated strength in several of them.

What your day-to-day will look like:

Vulnerability & Patch Management

  • Identify vulnerabilities in BMS/OT connected assets; plan and validate remediation paths using vendor resources and security advisories.
  • Test new software versions in a development environment; create and validate baselines prior to production deployment.
  • Execute patching across BMS supervisory devices (JACE/JENEsys), HVAC equipment controllers, and building technology applications.
  • Deploy approved software updates; support vendors and contractors through deployment; troubleshoot post-deployment issues.

Certificate & Credential Management

  • Renew and manage certificates for JACE/JENEsys devices, BMS supervisory equipment, HVAC controllers, and server infrastructure supporting BMS applications.
  • Sign and manage certificates for assets connected to the building/OT network; support certificate automation initiatives as they are introduced.

Product Onboarding & Technical Intake

  • Review and validate device onboarding and offboarding across diverse networks, including IP address, MAC address, and certificate signing.
  • Support new OT product onboarding end-to-end: lab testing, proof-of-concept validation, intake documentation, and asset scanning (e.g., Qualys, Tenable, or Phosphorus.io).

BMS Operations, Troubleshooting & Monitoring

  • Troubleshoot and restore BMS systems and services including offline and unresponsive assets; review system alerts and coordinate incident triage and resolution.
  • Monitor servers and storage supporting building technology applications; manage application backups and coordinate hardware replacements.
  • Respond to support requests from facility teams, property managers, and facility management partners; troubleshoot application and network issues affecting building technology operations.

Application Technology Ownership & SME

  • Manage overall technology health, stability, security, and compliance of BMS and building technology applications; oversee application lifecycle from onboarding through retirement and decommissioning.
  • Serve as the primary Subject Matter Expert (SME) for application support, governance, enhancements, and risk management; manage vendor relationships for application maintenance and upgrades (e.g., Siemens, Distech, Lynxspring, or other Niagara-based controls contractors).

Project Implementation

  • Support BMS controls cutovers, system startups, and new user group creation for new construction and retrofit projects.

Required Qualifications:

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Technical Management, or a related technical field (equivalent work experience will be considered in lieu of degree).

Technical Skills (depth in several of the following, not necessarily all)

  • 5+ years of hands-on BMS experience with expert-level familiarity with Niagara Framework (Tridium JACE/JENEsys).
  • OT network infrastructure: VLANs, LAN segmentation, DHCP/DNS, switch management, firewall rules, and secure remote access (VPN, ZTNA).
  • Vulnerability identification and patch management for OT/BMS assets; working knowledge of Qualys, Tenable, or Phosphorus.io; full software release lifecycle management (testing, baseline, deploy, troubleshoot).
  • PKI certificate lifecycle management for building control systems and supporting servers; compute infrastructure operations: server monitoring, backup management, DR testing.
  • Experience as a technical SME for BMS or OT application ownership, including compliance and lifecycle governance.

Process & Governance Knowledge

  • Experience submitting and tracking technology change requests in ServiceNow or equivalent ITSM platforms; familiarity with OT/IoT security frameworks (e.g., NIST SP 800-82).
  • Ability to navigate enterprise IT governance environments where OT/BMS intersects with corporate IT security policy.

Soft Skills

  • Independent, self-managing; translates technical findings into actionable items for non-technical stakeholders.
  • Vendor-neutral and collaborative when working alongside multiple integrators, contractors, and managed service providers.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Certifications: Tridium Niagara, GICSP, CompTIA Security+, or equivalent.
  • Experience with OT-specific asset discovery and vulnerability management platforms (Phosphorus.io preferred).
  • Background in financial services or other regulated enterprise real estate environments.

jobs.excerpt: About the RoleOur client — a physician-founded, venture-backed clinical AI research company (client identity confidential) — is building a system that compiles the standard of care into decision artifacts that execute at the point of care: schema-enforced, verified for exhaustiveness, and traceable to the source evidence that justifies them.
jobs.description:
About the Role

Our client — a physician-founded, venture-backed clinical AI research company (client identity confidential) — is building a system that compiles the standard of care into decision artifacts that execute at the point of care: schema-enforced, verified for exhaustiveness, and traceable to the source evidence that justifies them. Their compiler is live in public health care today, with clinicians acting on its recommendations daily.

This is a research role with production stakes. You will study how far frontier models can be pushed in extracting, structuring, and proving clinical logic, design the experiments that settle what works, and ship the winning approach into a live pipeline. You'll feel at home if you have published in clinical AI, want out of the demo cycle, and believe the logic behind a clinical decision has to be inspectable.

What You'll Do

  • Build the pipeline — convert clinical standards into executable modules: parsing with document and layout models, transformation, and validation.
  • Design the target syntax for representing guideline logic (exclusions, precedence, recommendations).
  • Run the experiments — open vs. closed models, fine-tuning, constrained decoding.
  • Co-design benchmarks — datasets, metrics, and error analysis for clinical fidelity.
  • Build adversarial cases that measure source fidelity, logical completeness, and recommendation correctness.
  • Develop deterministic validators using static analysis, constraint solving, or formal methods to make ambiguity, contradiction, and source silence explicit.
  • Turn model failures into hypotheses, experiments, and better system design.
  • Work directly with the founders and the clinicians who stake their license on the outputs.

Requirements (Must-Have)

  • Experience working in a frontier AI lab.
  • 3+ years of research or industry experience, or a final-year PhD/postdoc.
  • Shipped ML/NLP systems to production — not just research prototypes.
  • BS or higher in CS, ML, math, or a related technical field.
  • Production-level Python, PyTorch, and the Transformers ecosystem.
  • Experience with LLM evaluation, training, or prompt engineering.
  • Able to articulate failed experiments and uncertainty clearly in writing.
  • Willing to attend in-person offsites multiple times per year.
  • Authorized to work in the US or Canada — no visa sponsorship (potential exceptions for current employees of frontier labs).

Nice-to-Have

  • Compilers, program synthesis, formal methods, or static analysis.
  • Healthcare, safety-critical, or highly regulated domain experience.
  • PhD in CS, ML, NLP, formal methods, or statistics.
  • Knowledge of IR design, constraint solving, SAT/SMT, or DSLs.

Details

  • Compensation: USD $150K–$300K (higher possible for exceptional candidates), plus competitive equity (cash/equity mix is flexible).
  • Location: Fully remote, US or Canada, with offsites several times per year.
  • Type: Full-time.
  • Tech stack: Python, PyTorch, Transformers, LLMs, static analysis, SMT/SAT solvers, FHIR, HL7 v2.

IREN is building the infrastructure behind the next era of AI. We design, build, and operate massive-scale data centers, and we're racing to deploy some of the largest fleets of GPU and CPU compute on the planet. This isn't incremental growth — it's a full-throttle sprint to power the frontier of AI and high-performance computing. Our Network Sourcing team sits at the center of that mission, securing the switches, optics, fiber, and backbone infrastructure that let IREN's data centers come online and stay connected as fast as anyone in the industry.

The Role
IREN is looking for a Technical Sourcing Manager, Optics & Switches to take full ownership of our data center switching and optics category. This is not a support role — you'll be the commercial and technical owner of the switch, transceiver, and cabling relationships that let IREN's network keep pace with an explosive data center build schedule. If you love the adrenaline of a supply-constrained market, know your way around a leaf-spine architecture, and want to see your negotiations show up as switches racked and lit within weeks of your decisions — this is the seat for you. You'll operate with real autonomy, direct visibility to the Director, Network Sourcing, and the mandate to shape how IREN sources switching and optics at scale.

Responsibilities

  • Own switch and optics sourcing relationships end-to-end: commercial negotiations, pricing, quoting, contracting, and account governance.
  • Drive sourcing and procurement of top-of-rack, leaf, and spine switching, optical transceivers, and DAC/AOC cabling for general data center networking.
  • Stay ahead of a tightening supply market: track switch silicon, optics, and component allocation, and get out in front of shortages before they become blockers.
  • Partner directly with Network Engineering, Data Center Operations, and Program Management to keep sourcing timelines locked in step with build and go-live milestones.
  • Lead RFQ/RFP processes, cost modeling, and total-cost-of-ownership analysis for switching and optics programs.
  • Negotiate master purchase agreements, pricing schedules, SLAs, and support/maintenance contracts that protect IREN's speed and margins.
  • Track switch and optics vendor and ODM/whitebox roadmaps closely and shape sourcing strategy around the next generation of platforms before the market catches up.
  • Own supplier performance — delivery, quality, escalations, and quarterly business reviews — and hold vendors to a standard worthy of IREN's growth.
  • Build and maintain demand forecasts with capacity planning to drive purchase order timing and volume commitments.
  • Hunt for cost-savings and risk-mitigation opportunities: dual-sourcing, strategic buys, contract restructuring — anything that gives IREN an edge.

Requirements

  • 7+ years of experience in technical sourcing, procurement, or category management, with direct experience sourcing networking hardware from a major switch OEM and/or ODM.
  • Proven track record sourcing switching/optics hardware in a data center, hyperscale, cloud, or AI/HPC environment.
  • Deep understanding of switch architectures (ToR/leaf/spine), optical transceivers (SFP/QSFP), and DAC/AOC cabling, including relevant standards and interoperability.
  • Demonstrated success negotiating complex commercial agreements and managing high-value vendor relationships.
  • Battle-tested experience navigating supply-constrained/allocation-based markets and building mitigation strategies that actually work.
  • Sharp analytical instincts — comfortable building cost models, TCO analyses, and forecasts under pressure.
  • Excellent cross-functional collaboration skills; equally at home with network engineering, operations, finance, and legal.
  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience).
Preferred
  • Existing relationships with major switch/optics vendors and ODM/whitebox suppliers.
  • Experience sourcing for AI/HPC infrastructure at scale.
  • Deep familiarity with data center commissioning timelines and how network hardware delivery integrates with provisioning and rack integration schedules.

jobs.description:
NVIDIA is looking for a Senior Cloud Infrastructure and DevOps Solutions Architect to join its NVIDIA Infrastructure Specialist Team. Academic and commercial organizations around the world are using NVIDIA products to redefine deep learning and data analytics, and to power next-generation data centers. Join the team building and advising on many of the largest and fastest AI/HPC systems in the world!

We are looking for someone who combines deep technical expertise with strong consulting and communication skills. This role will engage directly with customers, partners, and cross-functional teams to assess, architect, and guide the implementation of large-scale infrastructure projects. The scope spans system architecture, Kubernetes-based platforms, and automation—serving as both a trusted advisor and a hands-on technical leader. You will sit at the centre of NVIDIA's Cloud Partner (NCP) operating model, covering the full Day 1 to Day 2 lifecycle: taking a GPU cluster from hardware handover, through full-solution validation, to a production-stable platform running at maximum goodput. NCP estates are open-source-first and heterogeneous—upstream Kubernetes, KubeVirt, Slurm, Prometheus/Grafana, Cumulus/SONiC and a long tail of ISV software—so this role is deliberately tool-agnostic: you will meet each partner on the stack they actually run rather than on a single proprietary product.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Own full-solution validation on the partner software stack—the layer above hardware validation—including cluster-wide stability testing, real training-workload acceptance, and multi-day, multi-rack burn-in against agreed MTBI and goodput targets.

  • Minimise the time from cluster handover to first production workload, working across hardware bring-up, managed-service intake and the partner's own operations teams to remove duplicated validation and handover friction.

  • Own Day 2 production stability at fleet scale: monitoring, logging and workload orchestration, fault detection and remediation, preventive maintenance, and proactive firmware and field-notice rollout campaigns.

  • Assess customer environments and operate heterogeneous open platforms—upstream Kubernetes, KubeVirt, Slurm and GPU-aware schedulers—integrated with enterprise-grade networking and storage, and enable third-party ISV workloads on top of them.

  • Provide consultative guidance and hands-on troubleshooting across the full stack—bare metal, operating system, software stack, container platform, networking and storage—and support R&D, POCs and POVs validating new features, architectures and upgrade approaches.

  • Act as the technical leader for assigned accounts: run structured knowledge transfer and enablement, and produce runbooks, onboarding materials and best-practice guides so partner teams can operate advanced configurations independently.

What We Need to See:

  • BS/MS/PhD in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, or related fields, or equivalent experience.

  • 8+ years in managing scalable cloud environments and automation engineering roles.

  • Cloud, HPC & GPU Expertise: Proven understanding of networking fundamentals and data centre architectures, with hands-on experience managing HPC/AI clusters and NVIDIA GPU-accelerated infrastructure—deployment, driver and CUDA toolkit management, optimisation, workload profiling and troubleshooting across CPUs, GPUs and high-speed interconnects.

  • Kubernetes & AI/ML Workloads: Extensive background with Kubernetes for container orchestration, resource scheduling and scaling in GPU-accelerated and HPC environments, including scheduler internals, batch schedulers such as Slurm, and mixed bare-metal/virtualised (e.g. KubeVirt) multi-tenant estates.

  • Linux & Storage Systems: Deep knowledge of Linux (RedHat, Ubuntu), OS-level security, and protocols. Experience with storage solutions such as Lustre, GPFS, ZFS, XFS, and emerging Kubernetes storage technologies.

  • Automation, GitOps & Observability: Proficiency in Python and Bash scripting, configuration management and Infrastructure-as-Code tools (e.g. Ansible, Terraform), GitOps-based cluster lifecycle and upgrade management for large fleets, and observability stacks (Grafana, Loki, Prometheus) for monitoring, logging and building fault-tolerant systems.

  • Fleet Reliability & Customer Engagement: Demonstrated ability to measure and improve MTBI and job goodput on large GPU clusters—fault detection, drain and remediation workflows, SLO/error-budget definition and post-incident review—combined with a strong consultative background leading architectural reviews and presenting to executive stakeholders.

Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:

  • Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and container-based microservices architectures for software deployment and automation.

  • Experience with the NVIDIA GPU and Network Operators for automated GPU and network resource lifecycle management in Kubernetes, and with NVIDIA Base Command Manager (BCM) for provisioning, managing and monitoring GPU clusters at scale.

  • Familiarity with GPU health and fleet telemetry tooling—DCGM and XID diagnostics, node-level health agents, and fleet-wide reliability intelligence.

  • Expertise in AI-native scheduling and inference frameworks on Kubernetes (e.g. KAI, Grove, Dynamo, NVIDIA Cloud Functions).

  • Background with RDMA-based fabrics (InfiniBand or RoCE) in HPC or AI environments. Exposure to Cumulus Linux, SONiC or Spectrum-X fabrics, DPU/DOCA infrastructure services, and NVLink/NVSwitch partition operations (NMX-C / NMX-M) on NVL72-class systems is a strong plus.

Role Description

As a GTM Readiness Manager within the GTM organization, you will help turn product and business changes into executable go-to-market motions. You will work across Product, Sales, Marketing, Customer Experience, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, Enablement, and Technology to ensure the business is operationally ready to bring new products, packaging, and other commercial changes to market.

You will play a critical role in translating product decisions into GTM requirements, identifying cross-functional dependencies, coordinating operational readiness, and ensuring the end-to-end customer and seller experience works as intended. This role sits at the intersection of product and commercial execution, giving you broad exposure across the business and the opportunity to improve how we bring increasingly complex products and commercial models to market.

You will serve as a critical connection point between Product and the teams responsible for bringing product changes to market, ensuring teams are aligned and operationally ready for launch. You will also help build and scale the GTM Readiness capability, creating clearer processes, identifying dependencies earlier, reducing launch friction, and enabling teams to move faster and execute with greater confidence.

Responsibilities

  • Own GTM readiness for product and commercial changes, including new product launches, pricing and packaging changes, new SKUs, migrations, deprecations, and changes to routes to market.
  • Translate product decisions into commercial and operational requirements across areas such as product catalog, pricing and approvals, contracting, Salesforce/CPQ, billing and ordering, provisioning and entitlements, compensation, reporting, and customer lifecycle.
  • Partner with Product teams early in the development lifecycle to understand upcoming changes, identify impacted GTM motions, and establish the decisions, owners, dependencies, and lead times required for readiness.
  • Orchestrate cross-functional readiness across Product, Sales, Marketing, Customer Experience, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, Enablement, GTM Technology, and other impacted teams, while maintaining clear accountability with the teams that own individual decisions and deliverables.
  • Drive end-to-end operational validation, defining critical business scenarios and ensuring appropriate owners validate the complete customer and seller experience across quoting, ordering, provisioning, billing, reporting, renewal, support, and other applicable workflows.
  • Identify and manage readiness risks, surfacing unresolved decisions, dependencies, and operational gaps early and driving them toward resolution or explicit risk acceptance before launch.
  • Improve the GTM Readiness operating model by creating reusable processes, launch patterns, requirements frameworks, and automation that reduce manual coordination and make future launches faster and more predictable.

Requirements

  • At least 8 years of overall professional experience.
  • 5+ years of experience in Product Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Commercial Operations, Business Systems, or another role supporting complex cross-functional GTM initiatives.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting product launches, pricing/packaging changes, commercial model changes, or other initiatives requiring coordination between Product and GTM teams.
  • Working knowledge of core SaaS commercial processes, including multiple areas such as opportunity-to-order, quoting/CPQ, pricing, contracting, billing, provisioning, renewals, compensation, or customer lifecycle management.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous product or business needs into clear operational requirements, dependencies, decisions, and execution plans.
  • Experience independently coordinating complex initiatives across Product, Technology, Finance, Legal, Sales, and other business functions without direct authority over participating teams.
  • Strong systems thinking, with the ability to understand how a change in one part of the commercial lifecycle can affect downstream processes, systems, data, and customer experiences.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience documenting requirements, facilitating cross-functional decisions, communicating risks, and driving clarity among stakeholders with different priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working in a B2B SaaS or subscription-based business with multiple products, customer segments, or routes to market.
  • Experience with Salesforce, CPQ, billing, commerce, provisioning, entitlement, or other systems supporting the quote-to-cash/customer lifecycle.
  • Experience designing or improving product launch, commercialization, or GTM readiness processes rather than solely executing within an established process.
  • Experience supporting products sold through multiple motions, such as self-service, direct sales, channel, reseller, or partner ecosystems.
  • Familiarity with automation and AI capabilities that can simplify requirements gathering, dependency management, testing, and operational readiness.

Durable Skills

AI fluency means using these tools to amplify human judgment, not replace it. We believe people with these skills will thrive as work and technologycontinue to evolve:

  • Awareness:Understand yourself and others.
  • Judgment:Evaluate information and make decisions in complex situations.
  • Adaptability:Learn, adjust, and stay effective through change.

jobs.description:
Are you someone who can spot a winning YouTube angle before anyone else does?🎯

We're looking for someone who wants to build YouTube channels from scratch and watch them take off. You'll spot the topics and keywords worth chasing, launch new channels, produce content at scale, own the SEO and rankings, and keep testing until you find what actually works.

This is not a traditional content creator role. You’re expected to think like a YouTube growth/product manager, not just produce videos. You'd be joining our YouTube department, a fully remote team that builds and grows channels across several markets, inside a digital media company that's been ranking content through SEO for years. 🚀

🏆 Our playing field is iGaming (online casino) one of the most competitive markets out there, and for that exact reason, one of the most rewarding.

The role

It starts before any video exists: finding the keywords worth going after and studying what competitors rank for and why.
From there, you produce at scale: ideas, scripts, voice-over, thumbnails, publishing. Often remixing what you already have to test a new angle, rather than starting from a blank page.

Once channels are live, the work turns analytical: rankings, CTR, retention, signups. You read them and decide the next move.
Most tests won't work: That's the job. What matters is how fast you learn, and how quickly you scale what lands.

You'll use AI and automation throughout, and work within YouTube's policies as a regulated industry.

Where you'll spend your time:

  • Finding opportunities: keywords, search intent, competitors, channel angles
  • Building and producing: channels, content at scale, packaging
  • Outranking the competition: SEO, positions, CTR, retention
  • Converting: turning views into signups
  • Testing and adapting: scaling what works

Who we're looking for

We care more about how you think and what you can do than your degree or previous job title.

  • You're a heavy YouTube user and understand why some videos perform better than others
  • You're analytical and comfortable making decisions from numbers
  • You naturally think in terms of testing, measuring and improving
  • You're proactive and comfortable owning projects independently
  • You understand the basics of SEO, keywords and search intent
  • You're comfortable with content production and basic video editing
  • You already use AI tools and actively explore new ones
  • Excellent English, written and spoken

You'll launch things that go nowhere, and watch good ideas underperform for reasons you can't explain yet. The people who do well here keep adjusting, and read a failed test as information.

A strong plus: you've already built a YouTube channel, website, social account or other digital project. Didn't work? That's fine. What we care about is what you learned.

What we offer

🎯 Real ownership — your own channels, your own decisions, your own numbers.

🚀 A head start — years of internal tools, automation and market data, yours from day one.

📈 Performance over seniority — several of our team leads started here in junior roles.

🌏 Full remote — 35 hrs/week, flexible hours, at least 4 hrs overlapping Bangkok time.

🌴 Generous vacation leave

About GreenTomatoMedia

We're a digital media company based in Chiang Mai, Thailand, with 1,500+ websites across 8 languages, several million visitors every month, and a fast-growing YouTube department.

We don't work with clients or agency briefs. We build and grow our own products and brands, which means short decision cycles, real freedom to experiment, and the ability to see the impact of your ideas. 🌟

Our team brings together 45+ nationalities 🌎, and we believe a good idea should win because it works — regardless of who came up with it.
